title: A machine learning approach to MRI screening for brain arteriovenous malformations in hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.
abstract: Background Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) is an inherited vascular disorder characterized by telangiectasias and arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) in multiple organs. Although brain MRI screening is recommended in all patients with HHT, in many centers, this may be difficult to implement due to organizational constraints. The aim of this study was to develop a machine learning model to predict the presence of bAVMs and other cerebrovascular malformations in patients with HHT, with the goal of supporting risk stratification in centers where genotype information is already available and identifying patients who may benefit from closer and more conservative surveillance. Methods All patients with confirmed diagnosis of HHT, complete genetic work-up, and radiological screening (2018-2026) were included for the analysis. Two end points were defined: probability of detecting bAVMs, and probability of detecting any cerebrovascular findings. Analysis was performed using Python and R. Results A total of 142 patients with confirmed HHT (meeting ≥ 3 Curaçao criteria) were included. For bAVM prediction, both models showed good discrimination, with an AUC of 0.84 (95% CI: 0.73-0.94) for Logistic Regression (LR) and 0.85 (95% CI: 0.74-0.96) for Random Forest (RF). Despite the slightly higher AUC, RF showed lower specificity, PPV, and F1 score, higher sensitivity (0.73 vs. 0.69) and same NPV. LR also showed better calibration, with an intercept of -0.30 (95% CI: -1.38-0.78) and slope of 0.87 (95% CI: 0.34-1.40), compared with 1.39 (95% CI: -0.46-3.23) and 2.39 (95% CI: 0.64-4.15), respectively, for RF. In contrast, models predicting overall cerebrovascular malformations showed limited discrimination and poor calibration with both LR and RF. For bAVM prediction, LR identified deletion mutations, ENG, family history, ACVRL1, and truncated variants as the most influential features, while RF SHAP analysis highlighted ACVRL1, ENG, age, pulmonary AVMs, and family history. Conclusion Effective risk stratification was achieved by the phenotype-specific bAVM model, supporting its potential applicability. Upon external validation this tool may enable an efficient allocation of screening strategies.

title: Structural brain changes in age-related macular degeneration before and 6 months after Scharioth macula lens implantation: an exploratory MRI study.
abstract: Background and purpose Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is associated with visual impairment and with structural and functional brain differences. The extent of these differences and whether longitudinal structural changes are detectable after visual rehabilitation, including implantation of the Scharioth macula lens (SML), remain incompletely understood. This study aimed primarily to characterize baseline deviations from normative MRI reference values and secondarily to describe whether longitudinal changes were detectable after SML implantation. Materials and methods Ten patients with dry AMD (mean age 78.8 ± 5.6 years) underwent structural brain MRI at 3 T before and 6 months after SML implantation. Regional volumes and age-, sex-, and head-size-normalized normative percentiles were generated using the fully automated AI-assisted multi-atlas segmentation tool (cNeuro cMRI). All reported hypothesis tests used normative percentiles; absolute regional volumes were not used in inferential analyses. Analyses included baseline deviation in an anatomically defined visual-network family (k = 36), exploratory longitudinal visual-network tests (k = 36), an exploratory analysis outside that network (k = 221), and an exploratory reduced-dimension family of three brain and three quality-of-life (VFQ-25) composites (k = 6), with false discovery rate (FDR) correction within each family. Results At baseline, deviation from the normative median survived FDR correction for the left, total, and right occipital pole and the left lingual gyrus. Longitudinal visual-network observations were limited to uncorrected exploratory changes in the left middle occipital gyrus (p = 0.004, pFDR = 0.141), total occipital pole (p = 0.027, pFDR = 0.428), and left occipital lobe (p = 0.049, pFDR = 0.428); none survived FDR correction. No region outside the visual network survived FDR correction (minimum pFDR = 0.216). None of the six reduced-dimension composites survived FDR correction, and no exploratory structure-function association or regression coefficient was robust after correction or interval estimation. Conclusions Patients with dry AMD showed regionally selective structural deviations in the posterior visual cortex, particularly the occipital pole, relative to the normative MRI reference. No longitudinal finding within or outside the visual network survived FDR correction; the uncorrected regional observations were heterogeneous and are considered exploratory. Because the study was sensitive only to large within-subject effects, the absence of corrected structural change should be interpreted in the context of limited sensitivity and not as evidence that structural change was absent.

title: Photon-counting computed tomography improves interobserver agreement in the evaluation of failed stapes surgery.
abstract: Purpose Failed stapes surgery presents a diagnostic challenge requiring high-resolution imaging to guide revision. Photon-counting CT (PCCT) offers improved spatial resolution and reduced noise compared with conventional energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT). This study compared PCCT and EID-CT for identifying etiologies of failed primary stapes surgery, with emphasis on diagnostic accuracy, interobserver agreement, and interpreter confidence. Methods In this retrospective study, 38 patients with failed primary stapes surgery who underwent successful revision surgery and pre-revision CT were included; 18 underwent PCCT and 20 underwent EID-CT. Three expert reviewers independently determined the cause of surgical failure using intraoperative findings at revision as the reference standard. Diagnostic accuracy, interobserver agreement (Fleiss kappa), and reader confidence were compared between modalities. Results Overall interobserver agreement was higher with PCCT (κ = 0.75; 95% CI, 0.60-0.90) than EID-CT (κ = 0.44; 95% CI, 0.30-0.59), with non-overlapping confidence intervals for overall agreement and ossicular discontinuity. Consensus diagnostic accuracy did not significantly differ between modalities (88.9% PCCT vs. 85.0% EID-CT; p = 1.00), nor did interpreter confidence (4.33 vs. 4.17; p = 0.29). Conclusion In this small cohort, PCCT demonstrated higher interobserver agreement than EID-CT without statistically significant differences in diagnostic accuracy or reader confidence, suggesting more reproducible assessment of failed stapes surgery.

title: Hippocampal and subfield volume differences in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis: associations with lesion burden and regional MRI involvement.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate global and subfield-specific hippocampal volume differences in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (POMS) and to examine their associations with white matter lesion burden and MRI-visible hippocampal or temporal lobe involvement. Methods The cohort comprised 119 patients with POMS and 120 control participants in a retrospective cross-sectional design. Bilateral hippocampal and subfield volumes were obtained from 3D T1-weighted MRI using the fully automated Hippocampal Subfields Segmentation pipeline and normalized to intracranial volume. White matter lesion burden (total lesion volume, lesion count, and lesion load) was derived using DeepLesionBrain. MRI-visible hippocampal and temporal lobe involvement was assessed by blinded radiologists and related to ipsilateral hippocampal volume using mixed-effects models. Results Total hippocampal volume normalized to intracranial volume was lower in patients with POMS than in controls (3.14 ± 0.49 vs. 3.41 ± 0.29; 7.8% lower; p < 0.001). Bilateral cornu ammonis subfields (CA1, CA2-CA3, and CA4-DG) and the subiculum showed lower volumes after FDR correction. The most prominent standardized between-group differences involved CA1 and CA4-DG. Higher lesion burden was associated with lower bilateral and overall hippocampal volumes. Ipsilateral hippocampal volume differed significantly across regional involvement categories in both adjusted models (p < 0.001 for each). Direct hippocampal involvement was associated with lower ipsilateral volume than both no involvement and temporal-only involvement, whereas temporal-only involvement did not differ from no involvement. Conclusion POMS is associated with lower global and subfield-specific hippocampal volumes, with a non-uniform pattern across subregions. Hippocampal volume differences were related to both overall lesion burden and direct MRI-visible hippocampal involvement.

The most prominent standardized between-group differences involved CA1 and CA4-DG. Higher lesion burden was associated with lower bilateral and overall hippocampal volumes. Ipsilateral hippocampal volume differed significantly across regional involvement categories in both adjusted models (p < 0.001 for each). Direct hippocampal involvement was associated with lower ipsilateral volume than both no involvement and temporal-only involvement, whereas temporal-only involvement did not differ from no involvement.

Conclusion

POMS is associated with lower global and subfield-specific hippocampal volumes, with a non-uniform pattern across subregions. Hippocampal volume differences were related to both overall lesion burden and direct MRI-visible hippocampal involvement.

title: Outcome After Late Pulmonary Valve Replacement in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot.
abstract: The optimal timing of pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) in adults with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) and severe pulmonary regurgitation remains controversial. Current recommendations rely largely on right ventricular volumetric thresholds derived from cohorts undergoing intervention during adolescence or early adulthood, although their prognostic value remains debated. To identify predictors of postoperative morbidity and mortality after PVR in patients aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF, with a specific focus on invasive preoperative hemodynamic parameters. We conducted a retrospective single-center study including patients aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF who underwent surgical PVR between 2009 and 2018. The primary outcome was a composite endpoint including supraventricular arrhythmia, cardiovascular rehospitalization, or all-cause death during follow-up. Clinical, imaging, and hemodynamic variables were analyzed using univariate and multivariate logistic regression. Forty-eight patients (mean age at PVR 41 ± 9.8 years) were included, with a mean follow-up of 52 months. The primary outcome occurred in 23 patients (48%). Preoperative signs of advanced disease, including right heart failure, left ventricular dysfunction, and a history of syncope or ventricular tachycardia, were associated with adverse outcomes. Although right ventricular end-diastolic volumes were markedly increased in both groups, they were not associated with the primary outcome. Conversely, right ventricular end-systolic volume and, particularly, right ventricular end-diastolic pressure (RVEDP) showed stronger prognostic value. In multivariable analysis, RVEDP remained the only independent predictor of postoperative morbidity and mortality (OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.01-3.40; p = 0.04). In adults aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF undergoing PVR, elevated RVEDP is a key predictor of postoperative morbidity and mortality, whereas right ventricular end diastolic volumes on MRI are not. Invasive hemodynamic assessment may help refine the timing of PVR in this "senior" population.

title: The Lymphatic System in the Fontan Circulation: Pathophysiology, Imaging and Therapeutic Interventions.
abstract: The Fontan circulation, the definitive palliation for patients with univentricular hearts, produces a unique haemodynamic state characterised by chronically elevated systemic venous pressure, reduced cardiac output and the absence of a subpulmonary ventricular impulse. Because lymphatic drainage depends critically on the pressure gradient between the thoracic duct and the systemic veins, this physiology has profound consequences for the lymphatic system. Over the past decade, the lymphatic circulation has moved from being regarded as a passive bystander to being recognised as a central determinant of Fontan failure. Chronic systemic venous hypertension drives lymphatic overproduction and impaired central drainage, leading to progressive lymphatic congestion that manifests as chylothorax, protein-losing enteropathy (PLE), plastic bronchitis, lymphoedema and Fontan-associated liver disease. Advances in magnetic resonance (MR) lymphangiography, in particular dynamic contrast-enhanced MR lymphangiography and T2-weighted MR lymphangiography, now permit direct visualisation of abnormal lymphatic flow and precise planning of image-guided interventions. Percutaneous lymphatic embolisation and thoracic-duct decompression, together with surgical decompression procedures and, ultimately, heart transplantation, have shown clinically relevant efficacy in selected patients with complications refractory to medical therapy. This narrative review synthesises current knowledge on the pathophysiology, imaging and treatment of lymphatic complications in the Fontan circulation. Lymphatic involvement is frequent, under-diagnosed, and prognostically important; the integration of advanced lymphatic imaging and the consolidation of expertise in specialised percutaneous lymphatic intervention represent the most relevant advances of the last decade.

title: Evaluating the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence for pediatric appendicular fractures: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Pediatric fracture detection on plain radiographs can be challenging, and missed fractures can have important clinical consequences. Artificial intelligence has been increasingly investigated as a tool to support fracture detection in children. Objectives This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence models for detecting appendicular fractures on pediatric radiographs. Materials and methods A comprehensive literature search was conducted from inception through February 1, 2026. Studies evaluating AI models for detecting appendicular fractures in pediatric populations using plain radiographs were included. Pooled sensitivities and specificities were calculated using bivariate random-effects meta-analysis, and subgroup analyses were performed based on anatomical site, unit of analysis, and comparator type. Results Sixteen studies were included. Pooled sensitivity and specificity for standalone AI models were 92.0% (95% CI, 90.4-93.4%) and 87.9% (95% CI, 84.5-90.6%), respectively, with an hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) area under the curve of 0.96. Considerable heterogeneity was observed (I 2 , 49-78%). No significant differences were found between per-image and per-patient analyses (P=0.78). Differences in diagnostic performance among physicians using AI models, standalone AI models, and physicians without AI models were not significant (P=0.20). Fagan nomogram analysis demonstrated that at 50% pre-test probability, a positive AI result increased post-test probability to 90%, while a negative result reduced it to 7%. Conclusion AI models demonstrate considerable diagnostic accuracy for detecting pediatric appendicular fractures on radiography. Considerable heterogeneity and concerns regarding real-life implementation highlight the need for prospective studies with standardized methodologies.

title: Evaluation of the relationship between the anatomical and morphometric characteristics of the sphenoid sinus in the paediatric population.
abstract: Objectives The aim was to analyse the morphological characteristics of the sphenoid sinus in the paediatric population and the possible effects of sex and age on the prevalence of pneumatization. Methods Patients in the 0-16 age group were determined as the paediatric group, and patients 16+ years of age were determined as the control group. Sphenoid sinus measurements and pneumatization classification were performed by two maxillofacial radiologists. Sphenoid sinus pneumatizations are divided into three groups: sellar, clival, and lateral. Results Types of right lateral pneumatization show significant differences between age groups (P=0.023). Lat-D type was significantly more prevalent in control group, while Lat-B type was observed only in the paediatric group. Like the right side, left lateral pneumatization types also showed statistically significant differences between age groups (P=0.013). Lat-D type is significantly more common in control group, while Lat-C is more frequently observed in the paediatric group. In terms of symmetry, there is a borderline significant difference between age groups (P≈0.05). While the height of the sphenoid sinus exhibited a weak positive correlation with the length of the optic chiasm (R=0.273, P<0.001), the anteroposterior length and width of the sphenoid sinus both demonstrated moderate positive correlations with the intercarotid distance (R=0.333 and R=0.435, P<0.001). Conclusion Lateral pneumatization type showed significant age-related changes. Optic chiasm length correlated with sphenoid sinus height, while intercarotid distance correlated with both sphenoid sinus anteroposterior length and width.

title: Imaging evaluation of pediatric acquired hearing loss.
abstract: Pediatric acquired hearing loss represents a clinical challenge, requiring prompt diagnosis in order to optimize normal language and psychosocial development. This review outlines a practical imaging framework categorizing acquired hearing loss etiologies into opacified and aerated middle ears. High-resolution computed tomography (CT) is the gold standard for delineating osseous anatomy, including ossicular discontinuity, fractures, and congenital or acquired bone erosion. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides soft-tissue characterization, and can evaluate labyrinth contents, cranial nerves, and for intracranial complications; non-echo-planar diffusion-weighted imaging (non-EPI DWI) can help to identify cholesteatomas. By leveraging these complementary modalities, radiologists can establish a precise diagnostic roadmap to guide clinical management and surgical intervention.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of 3D MRI rendering techniques for evaluation of hourglass-like constrictions in Parsonage-Turner syndrome.
abstract: Objective To evaluate inter-reader agreement and diagnostic accuracy of curved multiplanar reformatting (cMPR) and maximum intensity projection (MIP) techniques for detecting hourglass-like constrictions (HGCs). Materials and methods Thirty brachial plexus 3-Tesla, 3D, 1-mm isotropic MR neurography (MRN) datasets (10 patients without and 20 patients with Parsonage-Turner syndrome (PTS) affecting the suprascapular nerve (SSN)) were retrospectively analyzed by four musculoskeletal radiology fellows for the number and severity of HGCs using both post-processing views in a randomized, blinded fashion. An experienced, attending radiologist served as the reference standard. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using Gwet's AC1 and intraclass correlation (ICC). Image interpretation time was compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Results Inter-reader agreement for HGC presence was substantial to almost perfect among fellows (cMPR AC1 = 0.7, MIP AC1 = 0.67) and when compared to the attending (cMPR AC1 = 0.67-0.83, MIP AC1 = 0.63-0.83). Agreement for severe HGC count was substantial to almost perfect (fellows: cMPR ICC = 0.65, MIP ICC = 0.79; vs. attending: ICC = 0.62-0.83, MIP ICC = 0.69-0.88), but poor to fair for mild HGCs (fellows: cMPR ICC = 0.23, MIP ICC = 0.26; vs. attending: ICC = 0-0.21, MIP ICC = 0-0.09). Sensitivity to HGC presence was excellent (cMPR, 85-100%; MIP, 90-100%), though specificity (cMPR, 50-100%; MIP, 40-90%) and diagnostic accuracy (cMPR, 80-90%; MIP, 76-90%) varied. The MIP method required significantly less interpretation time than cMPR (median: 33 vs. 104 s, p < 0.001). Conclusion High inter-reader agreement and sensitivity but variable specificity for HGC detection suggest both techniques are viable tools for MRN, with cMPR better suited for detailed HGC evaluation and MIP for initial screening.

title: Sports-related peripheral neuropathies in athletes: mechanisms, imaging evaluation, and sport-specific patterns.
abstract: Peripheral neuropathy in athletes is increasingly recognized as a significant source of morbidity, with injury patterns varying according to the biomechanical demands of specific sports. Although peripheral nerve disorders in athletes may result from acute trauma, they more commonly arise from chronic, repetitive mechanical stress inherent to athletic activity. Despite their frequency, they frequently remain underdiagnosed, as clinical manifestations often overlap with other musculoskeletal disorders. Mechanisms of injury include compression, traction, laceration, ischemia, and repetitive microtrauma. Distinct athletic modalities are associated with characteristic neuropathies reflecting sport-specific kinematics and loading patterns. Awareness of these biomechanical factors and recognition of typical clinical presentations are essential for accurate assessment of athletes with suspected nerve injury. Diagnostic evaluation frequently requires advanced imaging modalities, particularly magnetic resonance neurography (MRN) and high-resolution ultrasound (HRUS), which enable detailed structural assessment of peripheral nerves and detection of secondary imaging findings. Electrodiagnostic studies may provide complementary functional information in selected cases. Early and precise diagnosis is critical to guide management, facilitate safe return to sport, and prevent long-term functional deficits. While most nerve disorders respond to conservative treatment, severe, progressive, or refractory cases may warrant surgical intervention to restore function and enable return to play (RTP). This review examines mechanisms of injury, clinical evaluation, classification systems, imaging findings, and sport-specific patterns of peripheral nerve injury across diverse athletic disciplines.

title: Multifocal isolated bone involvement in Langerhans cell histiocytosis in a 6-week-old infant.
abstract: Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is a rare clonal disorder of dendritic cells with a wide spectrum of clinical and radiologic manifestations. LCH occurs most frequently in infants often manifesting in multisystem or cutaneous disease. Consequently, the isolated multifocal bone involvement seen in this case is an unusual presentation for early infancy. We report a case of a 6-week-old female infant presenting with feeding intolerance and decreased use of the right upper extremity, found to have multifocal lytic skeletal lesions involving the humerus, ribs, calvarium, spine, pelvis, and long bones without clinical or imaging evidence of skin, hepatic, splenic, pulmonary, thymic, gastrointestinal, or central nervous system involvement. Diagnosis was established via CT-guided percutaneous biopsy of a proximal humeral lesion, which confirmed Langerhans cell histiocytosis. This case highlights the imaging features of multifocal osseous LCH in early infancy and demonstrates the safety and diagnostic utility of image-guided long bone biopsy in this vulnerable population. Early recognition and tissue confirmation are essential to avoid misdiagnosis and guide appropriate patient management.

title: Multiparametric quantitative MRI in knee osteoarthritis: evidence and requirements for interpretation and reporting.
abstract: Quantitative MRI can characterize cartilage and other joint tissues beyond visible structural damage, but its contribution to individual management of knee osteoarthritis remains uncertain. This narrative review examines the evidence needed to interpret quantitative measurements, combine parameters, and report their uncertainty. An initial PubMed search in June 2026 was supplemented on 14 September 2026 by an updated PubMed search and broader Embase and Web of Science searches. Targeted full-text assessment addressed incremental value, outcome timing, validation, and measurement error. Selected development studies found better discrimination with integrated diffusion and relaxation measurements than with individual parameters, whereas other combined imaging models did not improve on simpler comparators. Longitudinal associations were outcome-specific, and independent external validation was limited. Treatment studies showed inconsistent agreement between imaging changes and symptomatic benefit. We propose a five-step interpretation framework that establishes the clinical question, verifies technical adequacy, assesses morphology and comparable reference data, evaluates measurement uncertainty, and separates observations from clinical inferences. Two hypothetical scenarios illustrate its application. Quantitative MRI currently provides its strongest support as a controlled research measurement. Demonstrated reproducibility, an appropriate comparator, and evidence of added decision value are required before a quantitative finding can justify patient-level diagnostic, prognostic, or treatment-response claims.

title: Calcified foraminal metastasis from ovarian low-grade serous carcinoma mimicking a nerve sheath tumor.
abstract: Ovarian low-grade serous carcinoma (OLGSC) is an uncommon subtype of epithelial ovarian cancer, characterized by an indolent clinical course with potential for late local recurrence and metastatic disease. Musculoskeletal involvement is rare. We report a case of late OLGSC metastasis presenting as a slowly growing, thoracic foraminal mass in a 55-year-old woman, 33 years after initial cancer treatment. Rising CA-125 levels prompted 18 F-FDG PET/CT, which revealed an FDG-avid mass in the left T9-T10 neural foramen (SUVmax 6.6). CT demonstrated foraminal widening and intralesional calcifications, while MRI showed a dumbbell-shaped mass extending into the epidural space and left costovertebral region, with heterogeneous signal intensity and mild diffuse heterogeneous enhancement. Retrospective review of a CT examination performed 12 years earlier revealed a smaller foraminal mass without visible calcifications. Given its location and morphology, the lesion initially suggested a nerve sheath tumor, while the presence of calcifications also raised the possibility of a chondroid lesion. Although nonspecific, calcifications are recognized in primary and metastatic OLGSC. The combination of increased FDG uptake and the patient's oncologic history, raised suspicion of metastatic disease. Image-guided biopsy confirmed metastatic OLGSC with psammoma bodies. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of OLGSC metastasis presenting as a slowly progressive, calcified paravertebral and foraminal mas mimicking a nerve sheath tumor. This case emphasizes the need for careful evaluation of atypical masses in patients with a history of cancer, even decades after initial treatment, and the importance of biopsy for diagnostic confirmation.

title: Explainable radiomics and clinical models for prediction of total knee arthroplasty in knee osteoarthritis: data from Osteoarthritis Initiative.
abstract: Objective To develop and evaluate MRI radiomics models, with and without clinical variables, for predicting total knee arthroplasty (TKA) within 9 years in patients with knee osteoarthritis. Materials and methods This retrospective exploratory study included 507 participants from the Osteoarthritis Initiative-Zuse Institute Berlin dataset with manually segmented knee MRIs; 66 underwent TKA. Four hundred radiomics features from bone and cartilage were combined with 13 clinical variables. Logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) were evaluated using radiomics-only, clinical-only, and combined feature sets in an 80/20 development-holdout analysis and stratified nested cross-validation. Preprocessing, feature selection, and tuning were restricted to training folds. Results On the held-out test set, radiomics-only LASSO had the highest observed AUC-ROC of 0.76 (95% CI, 0.61-0.88), followed closely by combined LASSO at 0.75 (0.61-0.87). Combined logistic regression and XGBoost achieved AUC-ROC values of 0.73 (0.60-0.86) and 0.72 (0.57-0.84), respectively. Differences among the leading models were modest. In nested cross-validation, combined LASSO showed the highest discrimination (AUC-ROC, 0.786 [0.722-0.841]; AUC-PR, 0.343 [0.239-0.451]; F1 score, 0.405 [0.321-0.481]), with modest improvement over radiomics-only LASSO (AUC-ROC, 0.781 [0.717-0.834]). Consistently retained predictors included femoral bone sphericity, femoral cartilage first-order skewness, and WOMAC disability. Conclusion MRI radiomics features, alone or combined with clinical variables, showed potential for predicting TKA risk. Performance differences among leading models were modest, and these exploratory findings require external validation before clinical application.

title: Synovial plica syndromes: a comprehensive overview from embryology to pathology.
abstract: Synovial plicae are folds of synovial tissue in the knee, hip, elbow, and shoulder, representing embryonic remnants of synovial septa. They are usually asymptomatic, but trauma, repetitive microtrauma, or prior surgery can render them thickened and fibrotic, producing pain and mechanical symptoms collectively termed plica syndrome. It is easily overlooked or misdiagnosed because the symptoms are nonspecific and other intra-articular disorders often coexist. This review addresses the embryology, histology, anatomy, clinical presentation, imaging, and treatment of synovial plicae across these joints, with emphasis on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features. MRI is the preferred imaging modality for evaluating suspected plica syndrome, characterizing the fold and associated abnormalities, and excluding alternative causes of joint pain. Pathologic plicae appear thickened and irregular, with increased signal intensity and frequently associated focal synovitis or adjacent chondral damage. Plica thickness alone has limited diagnostic value, as measurements overlap between symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals. Establishing a diagnosis of symptomatic plica syndrome requires correlation of the imaging findings with the clinical presentation. When joint effusion is absent, magnetic resonance (MR) or computed tomography (CT) arthrography improves delineation of the synovial folds and associated lesions. Plica syndrome occurs most often in young, physically active patients, and management is initially conservative. When symptoms are refractory, arthroscopic resection relieves symptoms, particularly when the plica is the only abnormality and the cartilage is preserved. Most outcome data derive from the knee and the elbow.

title: Clinical outcomes and safety reporting after image-guided and non-image-guided subtalar joint injections: a systematic review.
abstract: Background Subtalar joint (STJ) injections are used for chronic hindfoot pain but evidence comparing guidance methods remains limited. Methods This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Embase (via Ovid), Scopus and Web of Science were searched from inception to December 2025, and the searches were re-run in a broadened form in July 2026. Eligible studies included comparative studies, single-arm cohort or case-series studies with 10 or more procedures and technical/cadaveric accuracy studies reporting subtalar-specific outcomes. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data and assessed risk of bias. Heterogeneity and scarce direct comparison precluded meta-analysis. Results Seventeen studies were eligible: 12 reported clinical data and five reported cadaveric technical accuracy data only (one clinical study also contributed a cadaveric control arm). Denominators are reported in their own units and are not combined: the clinical studies contributed 129 patients (six studies), 100 injected joints (four studies) and 779 injections (two studies). Ultrasound, fluoroscopy and landmark-guided injection were each reported in five studies. No study of CT or SPECT-CT guidance provided a subtalar-specific outcome. Needle placement accuracy ranged from 68 to 100%, but difference in design, populations and confirmation methods prevented comparison between modalities. Conclusion STJ injections are associated with clinical improvement but evidence is predominantly observational and heterogeneous. Differences in reporting technical accuracy, injectate, clinical response and adverse events prevent comparison of guidance methods. No modality's superiority is established. Prospective comparative studies using standardised outcomes and consistent safety reporting are needed.

title: Synthetic CT from biplanar radiographs for patellofemoral anatomical assessment: development and validation of an adapted X2CT-GAN model.
abstract: Objectives Accurate assessment of osseous morphology is essential for the diagnosis and surgical management of patellofemoral instability. Methods capable of providing CT-like anatomical information while reducing radiation exposure are therefore of considerable clinical interest. This study aimed to validate the accuracy of radiography-derived synthetic computed tomography (sCT) generated by a deep learning model for anatomical assessment of patellofemoral instability. Methods A total of 210 paired radiographs and CT scans were retrospectively collected and randomly divided into a training set (n = 170) and a validation set (n = 40). A deep learning model based on the X2CT-GAN framework was used to reconstruct sCT volumes from anteroposterior and lateral radiographs. Two blinded readers independently measured tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance, trochlear sulcus angle, and Caton-Deschamps index on both sCT and real CT images. Reliability, inter-modality agreement, and threshold-based classification agreement were evaluated. Results All intra- and inter-observer reliability values were excellent. Inter-modality agreement was excellent for TT-TG distance and good for trochlear sulcus angle. Agreement for patellar height was good. The mean absolute error for TT-TG distance ranged from 1.24 to 1.38 mm. Agreement for threshold-based classifications ranged from substantial to almost perfect, with high specificity observed across all evaluated cutoff values. Conclusions Radiography-derived sCT demonstrated good agreement with real CT for both quantitative measurements and threshold-based classifications relevant to clinical decision-making in patellofemoral instability. These findings suggest that radiography-derived synthetic CT may represent a promising lower-radiation alternative for anatomical assessment of patellofemoral instability in selected clinical scenarios.

title: Progressive collapsing foot deformity: advances in weightbearing CT imaging and three-dimensional assessment.
abstract: Progressive collapsing foot deformity (PCFD) is a three-dimensional deformity characterized, to varying degrees, by hindfoot valgus, midfoot or forefoot abduction, medial column collapse, peritalar subluxation, and valgus instability of the ankle. Conventional weightbearing radiographs remain the cornerstone of imaging assessment, whereas weightbearing computed tomography (WBCT) enables multiplanar and three-dimensional analysis of osseous alignment and articular relationships under load. This narrative review summarizes WBCT-based methods for the assessment of PCFD, including two-dimensional measurements, three-dimensional alignment parameters, articular distance and coverage mapping, diagnostic performance, and automated segmentation methods. WBCT enables quantification of the different components of the contemporary A-E classification and is valuable for assessing peritalar subluxation and lateral impingement. The Foot and Ankle Offset provides a reproducible measure of global alignment, whereas middle facet subluxation and regional mapping more directly characterize local abnormalities in peritalar relationships. Available evidence indicates that class D parameters contribute to distinguishing symptomatic PCFD from asymptomatic flatfoot morphology. However, published diagnostic thresholds remain dependent on the populations and methods used and should not be interpreted in isolation as diagnostic or therapeutic criteria. Automation substantially reduces the time required for three-dimensional analyses, and initial predictive models demonstrate the feasibility of quantitative preoperative planning. However, interchangeability between methods, external validation of thresholds, establishment of normative values, and longitudinal associations with symptoms and clinical outcomes remain insufficiently established. WBCT should therefore be considered complementary to conventional radiographs and MRI. Its principal contribution lies in the multiplanar and three-dimensional characterization, under weightbearing conditions, of the osseous and articular components of PCFD.

title: Cystic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors: a practical imaging approach.
abstract: Cystic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (c-PanNETs) are an uncommon cystic phenotype of well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, accounting for approximately 7-12% of PanNETs in several surgical series, although reported frequencies vary according to the definition of cystic morphology and cohort selection. Retrospective studies suggest that c-PanNETs may exhibit less aggressive clinicopathologic features than their solid counterparts; however, their imaging appearance frequently overlaps with other pancreatic cystic neoplasms, particularly branch-duct intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms, mucinous cystic neoplasms, and atypical serous cystic neoplasms. Accurate preoperative recognition may have important implications for patient management and surgical planning. This review summarizes the imaging features of c-PanNETs across computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography, as well as the complementary roles of endoscopic ultrasound and somatostatin receptor PET/CT. Particular attention is given to arterial hyperenhancement of the cyst wall, septations, mural nodules, or residual solid components; assessment of communication with the main pancreatic duct; and integration of complementary imaging findings. Because these features are not specific, their interpretation in combination with lesion morphology and ductal relationships is emphasized. Practical approaches to differential diagnosis and common interpretive pitfalls are also discussed. The review further addresses emerging quantitative imaging techniques, including radiomics and artificial intelligence, while recognizing that evidence specific to c-PanNETs remains limited. A practical diagnostic algorithm and structured reporting checklist are provided to support systematic interpretation and multidisciplinary communication. Recognition of the imaging spectrum of c-PanNETs, combined with systematic assessment of enhancement characteristics, ductal anatomy, and complementary imaging findings, may improve diagnostic confidence and support appropriate patient management.

title: CT-fibrosis score: development and internal validation for identifying advanced fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
abstract: Purpose Advanced fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) involves metabolic and anatomic remodeling beyond the liver. We developed and internally validated an interpretable CT-based score integrating abdominal body-composition and organ measurements and compared it with the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index. Methods We retrospectively studied 151 patients with biopsy-confirmed MASLD (86 advanced [F3-F4], 65 early-stage [F0-F2] fibrosis). Deep learning-based segmentation quantified abdominal adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, bone, liver, and spleen measurements. The CT-Fibrosis Score was developed using repeated (50×) stratified 5-fold cross-validation, with imputation, standardization, and feature selection confined to each training fold and inner 5-fold cross-validation for hyperparameter selection. Performance was based on out-of-fold predictions and compared with FIB-4 using the DeLong test. Sensitivity analyses addressed missing data, age dependence, and ascites. Results Four features were consistently selected: age, bone-to-abdominal-cavity volume ratio, visceral adipose tissue (VAT) density, and spleen index. The CT-Fibrosis Score achieved an out-of-fold AUC of 0.77 (95% CI 0.69-0.85). Among 141 patients with an available FIB-4 score, no significant difference was detected between the CT-Fibrosis Score (AUC 0.76) and FIB-4 (AUC 0.79; difference - 0.03, 95% CI - 0.11 to + 0.04; p = 0.37); this comparison was not powered for non-inferiority. Adding the CT-Fibrosis Score to FIB-4 did not improve discrimination (AUC 0.80 vs. 0.79; difference + 0.003, 95% CI - 0.04 to + 0.05; p = 0.90), with the confidence interval excluding an improvement greater than approximately 0.05. Conclusion The CT-Fibrosis Score achieved moderate discrimination for advanced fibrosis but did not improve discrimination when added to FIB-4. External validation in an unselected population undergoing CT for non-hepatic indications is required before any opportunistic application.

title: Artificial intelligence methods for HER2 status assessment: a systematic review and diagnostic meta-analysis.
abstract: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is an important predictive and prognostic biomarker that guides targeted therapy, particularly in breast and gastric cancers. Conventional HER2 assessment using immunohistochemistry (IHC) and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) is limited by inter-observer variability, heterogeneous expression, and diagnostic complexity. This systematic review and diagnostic meta-analysis followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines to evaluate Artificial Intelligence-based HER2 assessment. Fifty-one studies were included in the qualitative synthesis and 14 in the diagnostic meta-analysis. Bibliometric analysis, methodological taxonomy, comparative evaluation, and pooled diagnostic performance were assessed, with study quality evaluated using QUADAS-2. AI methodologies have rapidly evolved from conventional machine learning and radiomics to deep learning, Vision Transformers, explainable AI, and multimodal frameworks, with histopathology and Magnetic Resonance Imaging. being the most frequently used modalities. Research activity increased markedly between 2023 and 2025. Pooled sensitivity was 87.8%, specificity was 83.5%, and Summary Receiver Operating Characteristic Area Under the Curve (SROC AUC) was 0.852 (95% CI: 0.801-0.881), indicating promising overall diagnostic performance. Deeks' funnel plot asymmetry test showed no significant evidence of publication bias (p = 0.14). However, heterogeneity warrants cautious interpretation of the pooled estimates. Heterogeneous datasets, limited external validation, and inconsistent evaluation methods remain important barriers to clinical implementation. Future research should emphasize multicenter prospective validation, explainable and multimodal AI, foundation models, federated learning, and evaluation in underexplored malignancies, including gallbladder cancer.

title: Multimodality imaging of hepatic cystic echinococcosis: diagnostic approach, differential diagnosis, complications, and post-treatment assessment.
abstract: Cystic echinococcosis (CE), caused by the metacestode of Echinococcus granulosus sensu lato, is a zoonosis that remains endemic across the Middle East, the Mediterranean basin, North Africa and South America, and the liver is the organ most frequently involved. Because serological assays are of limited sensitivity and specificity, imaging carries the diagnostic burden: ultrasonography (US) is the cornerstone for initial diagnosis, staging, treatment planning and longitudinal follow-up; computed tomography (CT) best defines anatomical location, vascular relationships, mural calcification and acute complications such as rupture and superinfection; and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) more faithfully reproduces US-defined staging morphology than CT and provides superior soft-tissue contrast for assessing biliary involvement and separating CE cysts from cystic neoplasms. The aim of this pictorial review is fourfold: to illustrate the US, CT and MRI appearance of each World Health Organization Informal Working Group on Echinococcosis (WHO-IWGE) stage of hepatic CE and to explain how stage assignment translates directly into a stage-specific treatment decision-anti-parasitic treatment, percutaneous treatment, surgery or watch-and-wait; to present, stage by stage, the hepatic lesions that mimic CE and the findings that discriminate them; to depict the wall signs of the CE cyst that become visible with high-frequency linear transducers, including the three-layered wall, adherent brood capsules and hydatid sand; and to review the imaging of complicated CE together with the expected post-treatment appearance, procedure-related complications and the imaging strategy for detecting recurrence.

title: Preoperative prediction of Ki-67 expression in hepatocellular carcinoma using multi-sequence MRI radiomics: a non-contrast approach integrating T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and apparent diffusion coefficient imaging.
abstract: Background Ki-67 is a key immunohistochemical marker of tumor proliferative activity in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, non-invasive assessment of Ki-67 status before surgery remains an unmet clinical need. This study aimed to develop and internally validate multi-sequence magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics models based exclusively on non-contrast sequences for preoperative prediction of Ki-67 expression. Methods This retrospective study included 91 patients with 97 pathologically confirmed HCC lesions ( high Ki-67, ≥ 10%, n = 55; low Ki-67, < 10%, n = 42). Three-dimensional volumes of interest were manually segmented on T2-weighted imaging ( T2WI), diffusion-weighted imaging ( DWI), and apparent diffusion coefficient ( ADC) maps, and 5055 radiomic features ( approximately 1684 per sequence) were extracted were extracted from the three sequences. After feature selection with Pearson correlation coefficient filtering and the Kruskal-Wallis test, three multilayer perceptron ( MLP) models were constructed: Model-T ( T2WI), Model-D ( DWI + ADC), and Model-M ( combined T2WI, DWI, and ADC). The models were developed with five-fold cross-validation in the training cohort and were evaluated in a held-out testing cohort. This was a single-center retrospective study, and validation was internal only. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve ( AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. Results No significant differences in clinical characteristics were observed between the high and low Ki-67 groups. In the training cohort, the apparent (resubstitution) AUCs of Model-T, Model-D, and Model-M were 0.715, 0.823, and 0.860, respectively (representing model fit rather than cross-validated performance). In the held-out testing cohort, the corresponding AUCs were 0.707, 0.692, and 0.716. In the testing cohort, Model-M achieved a sensitivity of 68.8%, a specificity of 53.8%, and an accuracy of 62.1%, whereas Model-D showed the most balanced performance (sensitivity, 68.8%; specificity, 76.9%; accuracy, 72.4%). The dominant features were texture features derived predominantly from the ADC sequence. The cross-validated training AUCs were considerably lower (range, 0.522-0.585). Conclusions In this single-center, internally validated study, non-contrast multi-sequence MRI radiomics models integrating T2WI, DWI, and ADC showed moderate discrimination of Ki-67 expression in HCC. The contrast-free strategy is potentially applicable to patients with contraindications to gadolinium and warrants external validation; These findings represent internal validation only and require confirmation in external, preferably prospective multicenter, cohorts before any clinical application can be considered.

title: T2-weighted MRI-based radiomics for preoperative prediction of homologous recombination deficiency status in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma.
abstract: Rationale and objectives The aim of this study was to explore the feasibility of T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) - based radiomics in preoperative prediction of homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) status in patients with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), and to establish a non-invasive approach for guiding individualized treatment planning. Materials and methods A total of 133 patients with pathologically confirmed HGSOC who underwent MRI scan (T2WI, T1-contrast enhanced) were retrospectively enrolled in this study. All patients were stratified into HRD-positive and HRD-negative group. These 133 patients (41 in HRD-negative group and 92 in HRD-positive group) were randomly allocated to a training set (n = 93) and a validation set (n = 40) at a 7:3 ratio. Three different models were constructed and evaluated: clinical characteristics only (clinical model); T2WI-radiomics features only (radiomics model); and a combination of them all (combined model). The predictive performance was evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and area under the curves (AUCs) were compared using the DeLong test. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA) were applied to validate the clinical-radiomic combined model. Results In the training set, the combined model achieved the best performance (AUC = 0.889; all P > 0.05). The radiomics model achieved predictive performance comparable to the clinical model (AUC of 0.762 vs. 0.790; P = 0.676). In the validation set, the combined model performed significantly better than the clinical or radiomics model (AUCs of 0.853 vs. 0.805 vs. 0.706; all P > 0.05). DCA demonstrated that the combined model achieved superior net benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities compared with the clinical and radiomics models alone. Conclusions Our research demonstrated that the combined model achieved the optimal predictive performance. It is feasible to apply radiomics to predict HRD status of HGSOC patients, which can further assist clinicians in formulating individualized treatment strategies.

title: Percutaneous and endovascular procedures in adrenal disease: indications, technique, and outcomes.
abstract: Adrenal masses are found on roughly 4-5% of abdominal imaging studies, and the proportion rises with age. Most are benign, non-functioning adenomas that need imaging characterization and hormonal screening but no intervention. The remainder, comprising metastases, adrenocortical carcinoma, pheochromocytoma and hormonally active adenomas, raise questions that computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging cannot always settle; in these cases image-guided procedures can help. Percutaneous biopsy is reserved for hormonally inactive lesions whose benignity imaging has not established and whose histology would change management. Adrenal venous sampling remains the reference method for lateralizing aldosterone excess in primary aldosteronism and therefore decides who is offered adrenalectomy, although success depends heavily on operator experience and local protocol. Thermal ablation has produced biochemical and blood-pressure responses in selected aldosterone-producing adenomas and local control of limited metastases, but the evidence is largely nonrandomized and does not establish equivalence with surgery. Transarterial embolization serves three purposes: hemostasis in adrenal hemorrhage, devascularization before resection of hypervascular tumors, and functional treatment of aldosteronism, now supported by one small randomized trial. Each procedure carries hazards peculiar to the gland (catecholamine crisis, adrenal insufficiency after bilateral treatment, non-target embolization) that shape patient selection and periprocedural monitoring. This review covers indications, technique, outcomes and complications for each. Surgery remains the treatment of choice for most operable patients. Interventional radiology is most useful when the indications for sampling, ablation or embolization are recognized early and discussed at the multidisciplinary meeting, not only after surgery has been declined.

title: Automatic generation of training data from dual-energy CT scans: a new approach to train renal vessel segmentation models.
abstract: Objective To investigate the feasibility of automatic training data generation using virtual non-contrast (VNC) images of dual-energy CT and to evaluate the performance of medical segmentation models trained on auto-generated data. Methods Training images were generated from contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) scans using VNC algorithm. Corresponding training labels were generated from iodine-density images via intensity thresholding. The paired VNC images and labels constituted the dataset (791 cases in total) for training non-enhanced CT (NECT) segmentation models. We attempted to train segmentation models with VNC images alone, as well as the combination of VNC and real NECT images. Results Models trained with auto-generated data effectively performed renal vein segmentation on NECT images, achieving Dice score of 69.60%. It identified 100% (70/70) vein main trunks and 54.5% (6/11) accessory veins in the test set. The models' performance on artery segmentation was not satisfactory, with Dice score of 44.56%. It only identified 41.4% (29/70) artery main trunks and 4.54% (1/22) accessory arteries. However, the combination of generated data and labeled data greatly improved model's artery Dice to 71.23%. Combined model identified 100% (70/70) vein main trunks, 98.6% (69/70) artery main trunks, 68.2% (15/22) accessory arteries and 63.6% (7/11) accessory veins. Its accessory artery detection is significantly higher than the model trained with labeled data (15/22 vs. 5/22, p < 0.01), closing the gap with human radiologist (15/22 vs. 18/22, p = 0.250). Conclusion VNC and Iodine-density images can be utilized to automatically generate training data for segmentation models. This pipeline shows promise for training segmentation models on NECT images.

Methods

Training images were generated from contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) scans using VNC algorithm. Corresponding training labels were generated from iodine-density images via intensity thresholding. The paired VNC images and labels constituted the dataset (791 cases in total) for training non-enhanced CT (NECT) segmentation models. We attempted to train segmentation models with VNC images alone, as well as the combination of VNC and real NECT images.

Results

Models trained with auto-generated data effectively performed renal vein segmentation on NECT images, achieving Dice score of 69.60%. It identified 100% (70/70) vein main trunks and 54.5% (6/11) accessory veins in the test set. The models' performance on artery segmentation was not satisfactory, with Dice score of 44.56%. It only identified 41.4% (29/70) artery main trunks and 4.54% (1/22) accessory arteries. However, the combination of generated data and labeled data greatly improved model's artery Dice to 71.23%. Combined model identified 100% (70/70) vein main trunks, 98.6% (69/70) artery main trunks, 68.2% (15/22) accessory arteries and 63.6% (7/11) accessory veins. Its accessory artery detection is significantly higher than the model trained with labeled data (15/22 vs. 5/22, p < 0.01), closing the gap with human radiologist (15/22 vs. 18/22, p = 0.250).

Conclusion

VNC and Iodine-density images can be utilized to automatically generate training data for segmentation models. This pipeline shows promise for training segmentation models on NECT images.

title: Peri-ablational contrast-enhanced CT radiomics for predicting early progression of hepatocellular carcinoma after microwave ablation: development and external validation of a clinical-radiomics model.
abstract: Purpose To develop and externally validate a peri-ablational contrast-enhanced CT radiomics model for predicting early hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression after microwave ablation (MWA) and to assess its incremental value over clinical predictors. Methods This retrospective multicenter study included 376 patients in training (n = 235), internal validation (n = 60), and external validation (n = 81) cohorts. Early progression was defined as local tumor progression or new intrahepatic HCC within 1 year after MWA. Radiomics features were extracted from 5-mm peri-ablational regions on multiphasic CT obtained 1-2 months after MWA. Six machine-learning algorithms and phase combinations were evaluated. The selected radiomics model was combined with independent clinical predictors. Discrimination, calibration, clinical utility, and model interpretability were assessed. Results The arterial-plus-portal venous phase (AP + PP) multilayer perceptron model achieved AUCs of 0.857, 0.815, and 0.903 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively, with performance comparable to the three-phase model. Log 10 AFP and tumor size > 2 cm were independent clinical predictors. The combined clinical-radiomics model achieved AUCs of 0.926, 0.884, and 0.963, respectively. In external validation, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were 84.2%, 96.8%, and 93.8%, respectively. SHAP analysis identified the radiomics score as the most influential predictor. Conclusion Peri-ablational AP + PP CT radiomics combined with AFP and tumor size demonstrated good discrimination for early HCC progression after MWA and may facilitate individualized risk assessment, pending further validation.

title: Noninvasive imaging biomarkers of chronic liver disease severity and prognosis.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate whether MRI-derived functional and morphologic biomarkers are associated with clinical severity and prognosis in chronic liver disease (CLD). Materials and methods In this retrospective single-center study, 165 adults with chronic liver disease (CLD) who underwent gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI were included. Functional Liver Imaging Score (FLIS) was assessed on 20-min hepatobiliary-phase images, and Liver Surface Nodularity (LSN) was measured on contrast-enhanced axial T1-weighted images using semi-automated software. Spearman correlation analysis was performed for associations with Model for End-Stage Liver Disease 3.0 (MELD 3.0), and Albumin-Bilirubin score (ALBI). Time-to-event analyses for liver transplantation or death within 4 years were performed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to evaluate the performance of FLIS for predicting 1-year transplant-free survival (TFS). Results FLIS showed moderate inverse correlations with MELD 3.0 (ρ = - 0.532, p < 0.001) and ALBI score (ρ = - 0.541, p < 0.001). LSN showed weak positive correlations with MELD 3.0 (ρ = 0.154, p = 0.049) and ALBI score (ρ = 0.184, p = 0.018). In univariable Cox analysis, older age, lower FLIS, higher MELD 3.0, higher ALBI score, and LSN cutoff ≥ 3 were associated with a higher risk of liver transplantation/death. In multivariable analysis, age (hazard ratio (HR), 1.05; p < 0.001), MELD 3.0 (HR, 1.08; p = 0.003) and FLIS group (0-3 vs 4-6 points; HR, 2.39; p = 0.007) remained independently associated with liver transplantation or death. For 1-year TFS, FLIS with an optimal cutoff of ≤ 3 yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.71 (95% confidence interval (CI), 0.61-0.82). Conclusion Our findings suggest that MRI-derived functional and morphologic biomarkers, particularly FLIS, may provide noninvasive imaging markers of disease severity and prognosis in patients with CLD. Prospective studies with long-term clinical outcomes are needed to define their role in risk stratification and transplant decision-making.

title: Ultrasound-derived fat fraction and shear wave elastography for liver assessment in bariatric surgery candidates: diagnostic performance and longitudinal changes.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the diagnostic performance of ultrasound-derived fat fraction (UDFF) and auto-point shear wave elastography (Auto-pSWE) in bariatric surgery candidates, identify biological variables independently associated with their values and monitor postoperative changes in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) patients. Methods This prospective study enrolled patients who underwent UDFF and Auto-pSWE examinations within 3 days before bariatric surgery (October 2023-February 2025), with intraoperative biopsy as reference. Diagnostic performance of UDFF and Auto-pSWE (which measured shear wave velocity, SWV) were analyzed by receiver operating characteristic analysis. Multivariable generalized linear models identified variables independently associated with UDFF and SWV. Postoperative follow-ups were conducted at 3 and 6 months in MASLD patients. Results A total of 237 patients (mean age, 29.42 ± 9.37; 98 men) were included. UDFF showed excellent diagnostic performance for steatosis grades (AUCs: 0.991 for ≥S1, 0.911 for ≥S2, and 0.831 for ≥S3), with steatosis percentage as the strongest independent correlate (partial R 2 =0.302). SWV exhibited moderate diagnostic performance for significant fibrosis (AUC = 0.752), with fibrosis stages and alanine aminotransferase showing similar independent explanatory power (partial R 2 =0.067 and 0.063, respectively). In 104 MASLD patients, median UDFF decreased substantially by approximately 80% at 6 months while SWV transiently rose at 3 months before returning to a level comparable to baseline at 6 months. Conclusion UDFF provides accurate assessment of steatosis and shows potential for postoperative monitoring, whereas Auto-pSWE demonstrates moderate performance for significant fibrosis and transient postoperative changes, supporting its complementary rather than standalone role.

title: Radiomics can predict high-risk infection stones in patients with urolithiasis.
abstract: Objectives Our study seeks to design and develop radiomics (Rad) models utilizing computed tomography (CT) images to predict the presence of high-risk infection stones ahead of the operation. Methods This single-center retrospective study enrolled 576 urolithiasis patients. Preoperative CT images were used to extract the Rad features. Subsequently, multicollinearity elimination and Lasso regression were applied for feature selection and the construction of the Rad-infection score in training cohort. The validation cohort was utilized to assess its predictive performance. Additionally, the DeLong test and decision curve analysis (DCA) were adopted to compare the predictive performance between the Rad-infection score and routine clinical biomarkers. Afterward, univariate and multivariate analyses were used to identify the risk factors for high-risk infection stones. Variables with P < 0.05 in univariate analysis were included in multivariate logistic regression to develop nomograms. The base nomogram was established with only clinical independent predictors, whereas the radiomic nomogram integrated these clinical variables with the Rad-infection score. Results The Rad-infection score, composed of 6 Rad features, could reliably predict high-risk infection stones (AUC Training cohort = 0.751, AUC Validation cohort = 0.734). As evaluated by receiver operating characteristic analysis (ROC) and DCA, the Rad-infection score showed favourable predictive performance and clinical benefit relative to routine clinical biomarkers. Multivariate analyses demonstrated that gender, URBC, urine culture, and Rad-infection score were independent factors for high-risk infection stones (all P < 0.05). The nomogram derived from the Rad-infection score demonstrated strong predictive value (AUC = 0.867). Its reliability was further verified by five-fold cross-validation (AUC mean = 0.849). Conclusion CT-image-based models can preoperatively identify high-risk infection stones in our cohort. The Rad-infection score outperformed conventional clinical indicators. The Rad-infection score and radiomic nomogram hold potential to aid clinical decision-making.

title: CT-based machine learning and multimodal prediction in acute pancreatitis: a narrative review.
abstract: Acute pancreatitis (AP) has a highly variable clinical course. This narrative review focuses on computed tomography (CT) radiomics, deep learning and clinical-imaging models for severity and adverse-outcome prediction, with clinical-only models as context. A targeted PubMed search checked on 16 October 2026, with a publication cutoff of 14 October 2026, retrieved 80 unique records; ten CT-informed exemplars and eight clinical-context studies were selected for detailed comparison. This is a representative, non-exhaustive synthesis. For severe AP (SAP) prediction, reported same-center internal or temporal areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) ranged from 0.852 to 0.894, and reported external-test AUCs from 0.887 to 0.916; one validation cohort of unconfirmed independence had an AUC of 0.920. These descriptive ranges do not establish model superiority or characterize all retrieved studies. CT protocols and input timing, endpoint definitions, sampling and validation designs varied. Predominantly retrospective evidence, uncertain prediction landmarks, incomplete calibration and threshold reporting, and limited prospective impact assessment constrain translation. Feature explanations describe model associations rather than causal intervention targets. Imaging artificial intelligence (AI) remains an adjunct to clinical assessment; independent validation, calibration, decision-curve appraisal and prospective workflow/outcome evaluation are needed before clinical-pathway integration.

title: Integrated radiomics-deep learning modeling of hepatic vasculature for enhanced noninvasive prediction of portal hypertension and high-risk gastroesophageal varices.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate whether CT-derived radiomics and deep learning features can improve non-invasive risk stratification of clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) and high-risk gastroesophageal varices (HRVs) in cirrhotic patients. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 454 cirrhotic patients from center A and 77 from center B. CSPH labels were available only for patients from center A. Patients in both centers with available endoscopic findings were classified as HRVs or non-HRVs. A dual-path modeling framework integrating radiomics and deep learning-derived features extracted from multiple major hepatic vessels was developed, and was compared with single-path (radiomics-only and deep learning-only), single-vessel, vascular geometric, and clinical-feature-based models. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results For CSPH prediction, the dual-path model achieved the highest AUC (0.892 vs. 0.678-0.870 for the other models; P < 0.05 for most comparisons). For HRVs prediction, the proposed model achieved AUCs of 0.790 and 0.782 in the internal and external test set, respectively. The proposed model consistently outperformed the single-path models (0.625-0.648; all P < 0.05), single-vessel models (0.526-0.642; all P < 0.05), the vascular geometric model (0.528; P < 0.01), and the clinical-feature-based models (0.327-0.728; P < 0.001 for the APRI-based model) in the external test set. Conclusion A dual-path model integrating multi-vessel radiomics and deep learning features demonstrates robust predictive performance for CSPH and HRVs in cirrhotic patients. This approach may provide a new non-invasive alternative for risk stratification and clinical management of portal hypertension-related complications.

title: Detection versus grading on prostate MRI: a multi-cohort study of diffusion, perfusion and implications for biparametric protocols.
abstract: Purpose Prostate MRI is shifting toward biparametric protocols that omit the gadolinium-based dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) sequence - a decision validated entirely on cancer detection. Whether these protocols preserve the ability to estimate tumor grade, the quantity that drives management, has rarely been tested. Using unsupervised MRI "habitats" as a transferable probe, we asked whether the diagnostic contribution of MRI dissociates between detecting and grading prostate cancer. Methods Unsupervised k-means habitats of within-patient-normalized T2 and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), plus semi-quantitative DCE maps where available, were defined on PROSTATEx (training), frozen, and transferred unchanged to Prostate-MRI-US-Biopsy (external; 614 MRI targets and 12,809 biopsy cores with per-core Gleason) and QIN-Repeatability (test-retest). Under patient-grouped nested cross-validation we compared habitat, whole-lesion and clinical models, benchmarked habitats against ADC, validated habitat-pathology concordance against these cores, and tested whether the contribution of MRI dissociated between detection and grading. Results Low-ADC habitats localized clinically significant cancer across the gland (odds ratio up to 3.05; two lowest-ADC habitats captured significant cancer at twice the random-sampling rate) - but did not exceed whole-lesion radiomics or the ADC value itself (area under the curve 0.69 versus 0.69, cross-validated in the external cohort; cores 0.58 versus 0.62). In 107 MRI-detected lesions, ADC no longer separated grade groups (p = 0.79), whereas DCE time-to-peak did, remaining associated with grade after adjustment for ADC, zone and volume (adjusted p = 0.006; likelihood-ratio p = 0.026), although out-of-sample prediction was weak (cross-validated κ 0.05). Conclusion Diffusion localized significant cancer, but mean ADC did not separate grade in detected lesions; perfusion timing was associated with grade, yet predicted it poorly and has not been externally validated. Whether omitting contrast forfeits clinically useful grading information therefore remains an open question, to be tested before contrast-free protocols are adopted where grade estimation matters.

title: When US and MRI disagree: association of pre- high-intensity focused ultrasound imaging discordance with technical, safety, and clinical outcomes in uterine fibroid ablation.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the prevalence of pre-procedural US-MRI discordance and its association with Society of Interventional Radiology (SIR)-standardized outcomes in patients undergoing US-guided high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) ablation for symptomatic uterine fibroids. Materials and methods 308 consecutive patients were included. Discordance was defined as mismatch in fibroid type, location, uterine position, or absolute volume percentage difference > 50%. Patients were stratified into concordant (n = 252) and discordant (n = 56) groups. Outcomes were assessed according to SIR domains: technical success (non-perfused volume ratio on day-1 contrast-enhanced MRI), technical efficacy (through six procedural surrogates as a whole: energy-efficiency factor, overall treatment time, cumulative sonication time, treatment intensity, average sonication power, and oxytocin dose), adverse events (SIR classification), and favorable short-term procedural outcome. Results Discordance occurred in 18.2% of cases. Categorical agreement was high, with Gwet's AC1 > 0.93, and volume agreement was good, with an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.773. Day-1 non-perfused volume ratio and technical-success thresholds were comparable between groups. In unadjusted analysis, the energy-efficiency factor was higher after discordant imaging (p = 0.024) and oxytocin use was shifted toward the 60 IU dose (p = 0.036). After adjustment, neither association remained significant (p = 0.191 and 0.228). Adverse-event profiles and the favorable short-term procedural outcome did not differ significantly. Conclusion In this study, pre-HIFU US-MRI discordance was not associated with clear differences in technical success, technical efficacy, adverse events, or short-term procedural outcomes. Recognition of discordance may still help inform procedural planning and patient counseling within SIR-standardized frameworks.

title: Reply to Letter to the Editor: Reconsidering the Mechanisms of Urinary Incontinence Improvement After Abdominal Body Contouring.
abstract: We sincerely appreciate the constructive comments from the corresponding author of the submitted letter regarding our recently published single-arm meta-analysis focusing on the impact of abdominal body contouring on stress urinary incontinence. We fully acknowledge the valuable insights raised on surgical heterogeneity, underlying pathophysiological mechanisms and outcome measurement standardization, and we would like to respond point by point. First, during our initial meta-analysis design, we attempted subgroup stratification by surgical modality. Unfortunately, we only included 5 articles, and the raw data extracted from included published studies lacked uniform individual patient-level surgical detail, which made reliable stratified quantitative analysis difficult. Second, due to the core objective of our original article focusing on pooled quantitative efficacy analysis instead of in-depth mechanistic exploration, the discussion on pathogenesis was concise. Third, we recommend to adopt objective assessment in the future studies like pelvic floor ultrasound examination to detect some anatomic changes after the surgery.Level of Evidence V This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each submission to which Evidence-Based Medicine rankings are applicable. This excludes Review Articles, Book Reviews, and manuscripts that concern Basic Science, Animal Studies, Cadaver Studies, and Experimental Studies. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine ratings, please refer to the Table of Contents or the online Instructions to Authors www.springer.com/00266 .

title: Association of Capsular Involvement with Delayed Re-intervention After Splenic Artery Embolization for Blunt Splenic Injury.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate whether splenic capsule involvement is associated with delayed re-intervention after splenic artery embolization for blunt splenic injury. Materials and methods This retrospective single-center study included 329 consecutive patients undergoing splenic artery embolization for blunt splenic injury (2017-2025). Capsule involvement was defined as a laceration reaching the splenic surface with capsular disruption or communication with the perisplenic space on contrast-enhanced computed tomography. The primary outcome was delayed re-intervention. Cox and Firth regression were performed, with interobserver agreement assessed by Cohen's kappa. Results Delayed re-intervention occurred in 26 patients (7.9%) at a median of 6 days; all underwent repeat embolization; none required splenectomy. Twenty (76.9%) were detected on routine surveillance computed tomography without preceding deterioration. Capsule involvement was present in 25 of 26 events. Initial computed tomography showed vascular injury elsewhere in 25 of 26 patients, but neither computed tomography nor angiography showed pseudoaneurysm or active bleeding at the eventual lesion site. Re-intervention occurred in 25 of 245 patients with capsule involvement (10.2%) versus 1 of 84 without (1.2%). Capsule involvement was associated with re-intervention (hazard ratio, 6.82; 95% confidence interval, 1.62-28.74; p = 0.009), but significance was lost after reclassifying two events. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were 96.2%, 27.4%, 10.2%, and 98.8%; pre-consensus agreement was 97.6% (Cohen's kappa = 0.938). Conclusion Capsule involvement was associated with delayed re-intervention, but the estimate was statistically fragile because only one capsule-negative event occurred. Surveillance-driven, single-center findings are exploratory; external validation is required before changes in surveillance practice. Level of evidence Level 3, prognostic study.

title: Circulating Biomarkers for Interventional Oncology: Current Status and Future Direction.
abstract: Biomarkers reflect underlying physiological or pathological processes and support disease detection, cancer diagnosis, treatment selection and prognosis, monitoring of therapeutic response, and identification of disease recurrence in interventional oncology (IO) care. In recent years, liquid biopsy of circulating biomarkers has emerged as a transformative approach in oncology. Given the growing role of IO in cancer care and the potential for circulating biomarkers to directly impact patient care in Interventional Radiology, this narrative review summarizes circulating biomarker types, current detection technologies and workflows, clinical applications in IO care, and next-generation biomarker modalities and detection instruments for Interventional Radiologists.

title: The tibialis posterior tendon revisited: a classification-based anatomical and radiological framework.
abstract: The tibialis posterior tendon (TPT) demonstrates substantial anatomical variability in its branching and attachment morphology, extending beyond the simplified concept of a predominantly navicular attachment. This narrative review critically reappraises the classification of TPT attachment patterns proposed by Olewnik and places it in the context of subsequent anatomical, radiological, and functional evidence. Later anatomical studies have confirmed extensive variation in the number, distribution, and surface area of TPT attachments and have identified configurations not represented within the original classification. These findings support the use of classification systems as structured descriptive frameworks rather than exhaustive catalogues of TPT morphology. Cadaveric imaging studies demonstrate that complex TPT branching and attachment anatomy can be depicted on MRI; however, individual anatomical types and subtypes have not undergone systematic radiological validation. Representative MRI examples are therefore included for anatomical illustration rather than as diagnostic criteria. The functional significance of individual attachment patterns and their potential relationship to hindfoot and midfoot joint morphology remain incompletely understood. Further anatomical, imaging, and biomechanical studies are required to determine whether specific TPT patterns have reproducible radiological or functional correlates.
