title: Milwaukee shoulder syndrome: a neglected and underrecognized basic calcium phosphate crystal arthropathy.
abstract: Milwaukee Shoulder Syndrome (MSS) is a rare but extremely aggressive form of destructive arthropathy, primarily affecting elderly women. Despite its distinct clinical profile, it remains an under-recognized and frequently misdiagnosed entity. This review synthesizes current knowledge on pathogenesis, clinical presentation, and diagnostic nuances of MSS to improve clinical recognition. The condition is defined by the intra-articular deposition of basic calcium phosphate (BCP) crystals, such as hydroxyapatite. These crystals trigger the release of proteolytic enzymes, leading to massive rotator cuff tears, superior migration of the humeral head, and rapid joint destruction. A hallmark of MSS is the "inflammatory paradox": a striking dissociation between severe structural damage and a non-inflammatory or minimally inflammatory synovial fluid profile (typically < 2,000 cells/mm3), which often is hemorrhagic. Diagnosis is challenged by the nanocrystalline nature of BCP crystals, which are non-birefringent and invisible under standard polarized light microscopy, requiring specialized staining (Alizarin Red) or advanced analytics for confirmation. Multimodal imaging is essential, with plain radiography showing advanced degeneration and MRI or CT delineating the extent of soft tissue and bony destruction. Treatment is currently limited to supportive measures, including recurrent joint aspiration, analgesia, and physical therapy. In advanced cases, reverse total shoulder arthroplasty remains the primary surgical intervention for functional restoration. As the aging population grows, increasing clinician awareness of MSS-particularly its unique synovial fluid characteristics-is vital for reducing diagnostic delay and optimizing patient care.

title: Multiparametric MRI to predict response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer: Are we ready for NacBI-RADS?
abstract: Objectives Accurate assessment of treatment response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in breast cancer (BC) is crucial for guiding surgical planning. While size-based criteria remain standard, they may underestimate therapy-induced biological changes. To develop and validate the neoadjuvant breast imaging reporting and data system (NacBI-RADS), a structured multiparametric MRI (mp-MRI) lexicon was designed to evaluate NAC response and support surgical decision-making. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 68 BC patients who underwent staging and post-NAC MRI, followed by surgery. mp-MRI examinations included contrast-enhanced T1, T2-weighted, and diffusion-weighted imaging. NacBI-RADS integrates four parameters: peritumoral edema, ΔADC (apparent diffusion coefficient change), post-contrast tumor size, and lymph node status (Node-RADS). Three independent breast radiologists evaluated all cases. Inter-reader agreement was assessed with Cohen's and Fleiss' kappa. Results Of 88 patients assessed, 68 were included. Residual disease was found in 43 patients (63%) and pathological complete response in 25 (37%). Most lesions were categorized as NacBI-RADS 1-2, while categories 4-5 were less frequent (12-15%). NacBI-RADS showed high diagnostic performance (AUC 0.942-0.960) with excellent reproducibility (κ 0.931-0.953). Lower categories were associated with complete or near-complete response, and higher categories with residual disease (p < 0.001). Conclusion This exploratory study suggests that NacBI-RADS may offer a standardized and reproducible mp-MRI framework for assessing NAC response. Further studies are needed to confirm its role in imaging-guided surgical planning. Key points Question Can a structured mp-MRI framework improve the accuracy and reproducibility of assessing BC response to NAC compared with conventional size-based criteria? Findings NacBI-RADS showed high diagnostic accuracy (AUC up to 0.960) and excellent inter-reader agreement, reliably distinguishing complete/partial-complete responders from patients with residual disease. Clinical relevance NacBI-RADS may support more accurate and reproducible response assessment after NAC, helping identify true complete responders and aiding safe, personalized surgical de-escalation strategies in BC management.

title: Deep learning-based segmentation of the ischemic core and severe hypodensity on noncontrast head CT compared with CT perfusion and diffusion-weighted imaging.
abstract: Objectives To compare the spatial overlap, imaging marker agreement, and outcome associations of acute ischemic regions of interest (ROIs) using deep-learning NCCT (DLNCCT) versus manual NCCT, CTP, and DWI-based segmentations. Materials and methods We trained a deep learning model to segment ischemic ROIs on admission NCCT (DLNCCT). DLNCCT was compared with manual NCCT, CTP (rCBF < 30%/38%), and DWI using the Dice similarity coefficient (mean ± SD), Bland-Altman analysis (mean difference [95% CI]), and concordance correlation coefficient (CCC). For each ROI, we compared NCCT imaging biomarkers: average lesion density (HU); modified net water uptake (mNWU in %); total volume (mL); and hypodense (≤ 26 HU) volume (mL). DLNCCT biomarkers were associated with reversed 90-day ordinal modified Rankin Scale (genOR [95% CI]). Results We used 218/762 train/test cases. Dice was 0.30 ± 0.30 between DLNCCT and manual segmentation, 0.22 ± 0.25 between DLNCCT-DWI, and 0.15 ± 0.22/0.21 ± 0.24 between CTP (rCBF < 30%/< 38%)-DWI. DLNCCT-DWI biomarker agreement was -1 HU (95% CI: -7; 6) for average density (CCC: 0.71), 4.9% (95% CI: -7.0; 16.8) for mNWU (CCC: 0.35), -16 mL (95% CI: -108; 76) for total volume (CCC: 0.57), and -4 mL (95% CI: -31; 23) for hypodense lesion volume (CCC: 0.75). Average lesion density (1.11 [95% CI: 1.06; 1.16]) and hypodense volume (0.85 [95% CI: 0.72; 0.99]) were associated with 90-day mRS. Conclusion Spatial and biomarker agreement between DLNCCT and DWI was suboptimal but comparable to CTP-DWI. Nevertheless, DLNCCT-derived average lesion density and hypodense volume were associated with functional outcomes. Key points Question Deep-learning models segment ischemic tissue on NCCT, but their spatial overlap and accuracy of imaging biomarker assessment relative to DWI and CTP core remain unclear. Findings Deep-learning NCCT segmentation showed good agreement with DWI in measuring hypodense (≤ 26 HU) volumes (- 4 mL [95% CI: -31; 23]; CCC 0.75). Clinical relevance Despite limited spatial overlap, NCCT-derived deep learning biomarkers showed agreement comparable to DWI, with improved performance in patients with poor ASPECTS and collateral scores. Hypodense volume and average lesion density were associated with functional outcome.

title: ESR Essentials: MRI of the scrotum-practice recommendations by the European Society of Urogenital Radiology.
abstract: While conventional ultrasonography (US) remains the first-line imaging modality for scrotal pathology, multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) has emerged as a valuable problem-solving tool for indeterminate US findings. Owing to its superior soft-tissue contrast, functional imaging capabilities, and operator independence, mpMRI allows for the precise localization and characterization of scrotal lesions. This paper from the European Society of Urogenital Radiology Scrotal and Penile Imaging Working Group provides a comprehensive, evidence-based overview of scrotal mpMRI for a general radiologist. It details optimized imaging protocols, recommending a standard sequence of T1-weighted, T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and subtracted dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging. The article highlights key clinical indications, including the characterization of intratesticular and paratesticular masses, local staging of testicular germ cell tumors, and differentiation between germ cell and sex cord-stromal neoplasms. This paper familiarizes radiologists with normal MRI appearances and MRI findings of common scrotal diseases. Evidence-based recommendations for reporting basic MRI examinations of the scrotum are also provided. The potential of advanced techniques, such as diffusion tensor imaging and proton MR spectroscopy, and the future integration of artificial intelligence and radiomics, are also discussed. We hope the implementation of these recommendations into radiological practice will enhance diagnostic confidence and promote standardized practice in scrotal MRI for radiologists. KEY POINTS: While conventional ultrasound is the first-line modality for scrotal pathology, it can yield inconclusive findings regarding complex mass characterization and local tumor staging. Multiparametric MRI combines anatomical and functional data to accurately characterize scrotal masses, localize impalpable, undescended testes, and provide precise local tumor staging. Scrotal multiparametric MRI serves as a valuable problem-solving tool that enhances diagnostic confidence in sonographically indeterminate cases, prevents unnecessary radical orchiectomies, supports testis-sparing surgery or active surveillance, and standardizes radiological reporting templates to optimize personalized patient management.

title: Comprehensive multi-organ and body composition phenotyping identifies metabolic signatures associated with incident type 2 diabetes.
abstract: Objectives To derive a multi-organ imaging biomarker panel from whole-body MRI and evaluate its predictive value for incident type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), including the role of intermuscular adipose tissue (IMAT) in reconciling discrepancies between muscle volume and metabolic risk. Materials and methods This retrospective cohort study analyzed 46,129 UK Biobank participants without diabetes at the time of imaging. Organ volume indices and fat fractions were extracted from Dixon MRI through automated segmentation. Associations between muscle volume indices, fat fractions, and handgrip strength were evaluated, and IMAT was graded in strength-matched participants. Independent imaging biomarkers were identified using adjusted Cox models, and a deep learning model was trained. Added value relative to the Leicester risk assessment score was evaluated using decision curve analysis. Results During follow-up, 600 participants developed T2DM. Eight biomarkers independently predicted incident T2DM, including liver volume index (hazard ratio (HR), 1.28; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.19-1.38), pancreas fat fraction (HR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.10-1.28), and gluteus fat fraction (HR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.08-1.27). Gluteal IMAT grades were higher in weak-for-volume participants than in strength-matched controls (median, 2.0 vs 1.0; p = 0.02). The deep learning model achieved a concordance index of 0.814 (95% CI, 0.797-0.832) and, when applied sequentially with clinical criteria, reduced false-positive classifications by 43.0% while preserving 97.3% of true positives. Conclusion Whole-body MRI-derived multi-organ biomarkers independently predicted incident T2DM and enhanced risk stratification beyond an established clinical risk score. Muscle fat fraction may better reflect metabolic risk than muscle volume in IMAT-rich regions. Key points Question Clinical risk scores miss the multi-organ pathophysiology of type 2 diabetes; does whole-body MRI organ size and fat quantification improve prediction of incident diabetes? Findings Eight MRI-derived biomarkers independently predicted incident type 2 diabetes; a deep learning model using whole-body MRI biomarkers reached a concordance index of 0.814. Clinical relevance Automated whole-body MRI biomarkers capture multi-organ metabolic signatures beyond conventional risk scoring. Applied after clinical screening, they remove 43.0% of false-positive classifications while preserving 97.3% of true positives.

title: Reducing operator-dependent variability in liver shear wave elastography through an AI-guided region-of-interest placement pipeline.
abstract: Objectives To develop and evaluate an artificial intelligence (AI) pipeline that automates optimal circular region-of-interest (ROI) placement and the surrounding elastogram box, provides probe-angle/contact guidance, and measures skin-to-capsule distance (SCD) to standardize liver SWE acquisition, aiming to reduce operator-dependent variability. Materials and methods A two-stage pipeline combined SimCLR self-supervised pretraining on 17,441 unlabeled ultrasound images, followed by ENet fine-tuning using 495 annotated images for liver segmentation and 1564 images for poor probe contact detection. Segmentation outputs were combined with constraints on valid liver tissue pixels, axial depth, lateral boundaries, and regions of poor acoustic coupling to generate masks for optimal ROI placement. A distance transformation algorithm then identified optimal ROI coordinates within these masks. An inter-observer reader study assessed AI performance by comparing automated ROI placement, SCD measurements, and probe-angle correction guidance with annotations from expert attending radiologists. Results 18,182 US images from 654 liver elastography examinations in 609 patients (mean age, 52.6 ± 12.95 years; 55.4% male) were acquired from three ultrasound systems. The AI pipeline achieved liver segmentation performance with a Dice coefficient of 0.89, sensitivity of 0.95, specificity of 0.93, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.94. The reader study demonstrated significantly higher AI-to-attending radiologist agreement (93.8%) compared to inter-attending agreement for ROI placement (81%). Cohen's kappa agreement between two attending radiologists was 0.25. Conclusion The proposed AI-driven pipeline significantly improved ROI placement consistency and reproducibility, highlighting its potential to enhance clinical reliability in liver fibrosis assessment. Key points Question Operator-dependent variability in region-of-interest (ROI) placement compromises measurement reproducibility in B-mode shear wave elastography. We developed an AI pipeline to place an optimal ROI. Findings The AI pipeline achieved liver segmentation performance of Dice 0.89 (AUC 0.94) and demonstrated higher AI-to-attending agreement (93.8%) than inter-attending agreement (81%) for ROI placement. Clinical relevance By standardizing ROI placement, elastogram box selection, and probe angle/contact guidance, the AI pipeline reduces operator-dependent variability in liver SWE acquisition, supporting more reproducible liver stiffness measurements that could improve fibrosis staging reliability.

title: An integrated MRI-pathology model for predicting response to TACE combined with targeted therapy and immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Objectives The efficacy of transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by variable responses. We aimed to develop and validate an integrated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-pathology model for response prediction and survival stratification (IMPRESS), which combines pretreatment MRI habitat radiomics and paired biopsy whole-slide images (WSIs) pathomics. Materials and methods This multicenter, retrospective study enrolled patients with unresectable HCC receiving TACE plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy from January 2019 to December 2024. Eligibility required pretreatment MRI and paired biopsy WSIs within 1 month before therapy, Child-Pugh class A/B, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status ≤ 1, and at least one measurable intrahepatic lesion ≥ 1 cm. Patients with missing or poor-quality MRI or WSIs, prior locoregional or systemic HCC therapy, second malignancy, ECOG ≥ 2, or incomplete data were excluded. Habitat MRI radiomics, WSI pathomics, and clinical features were integrated into IMPRESS. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Single-cell analysis was performed to explore the biological basis of the IMPRESS predictions. Results Among 231 patients, 94 (40.7%) achieved a treatment response. IMPRESS achieved AUCs of 0.957 (95% CI: 0.931-1.0), 0.878 (95% CI: 0.789-0.966), and 0.875 (95% CI: 0.782-0.966) in the training, validation, and test cohorts, respectively. Predicted responders and non-responders showed significantly different overall survival in all cohorts (all p < 0.001). Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed distinct immune and proliferative patterns consistent with model predictions. Conclusion IMPRESS model may provide a promising tool for pretreatment response prediction and survival risk stratification in unresectable HCC undergoing TACE-based combination therapy. Objectives

The efficacy of transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by variable responses. We aimed to develop and validate an integrated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-pathology model for response prediction and survival stratification (IMPRESS), which combines pretreatment MRI habitat radiomics and paired biopsy whole-slide images (WSIs) pathomics.

This multicenter, retrospective study enrolled patients with unresectable HCC receiving TACE plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy from January 2019 to December 2024. Among 231 patients, 94 (40.7%) achieved a treatment response. Predicted responders and non-responders showed significantly different overall survival in all cohorts (all p < 0.001). Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed distinct immune and proliferative patterns consistent with model predictions.

Conclusion

IMPRESS model may provide a promising tool for pretreatment response prediction and survival risk stratification in unresectable HCC undergoing TACE-based combination therapy.

Key points

Question Reliable pretreatment tools are needed to identify unresectable HCC patients likely to benefit from TACE plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy. Findings An integrated MRI-pathology model combining habitat radiomics and deep-learning pathomics predicted treatment response, with validation and testing areas under the curve of 0.878 and 0.875. Clinical relevance The integrated model may support pretreatment response stratification for TACE-based triple therapy and help inform surveillance intensity or alternative treatment considerations, pending prospective validation.

title: A fractal-integrated CT score predicts high-risk pathology and early recurrence in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Objective To develop and validate a noninvasive CT-based imaging score incorporating fractal analysis to predict high-risk pathological features in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and to assess its prognostic value for early recurrence. Materials and methods This retrospective bicenter study included 514 patients with pathologically confirmed PDAC who underwent curative resection, divided into training (n = 219), internal validation (n = 94), external validation (n = 100) and outcome datasets (n = 101). The fractal dimension (FD) and lacunarity were extracted from portal venous-phase CT images via box-counting algorithms. Imaging predictors of high-risk pathological features, including high tumor grade, lymphovascular invasion (LVI) and perineural invasion (PNI), were identified by logistic regression and integrated into a comprehensive weighted imaging score. Cox regression analyses were performed to assess its prognostic value for early recurrence. Results Patients with high-risk pathological features exhibited greater FD and lacunarity. The final score included six imaging features: necrosis, peripancreatic fat infiltration, venous involvement, regional lymphadenopathy, FD and lacunarity. For any high-risk pathology, the fractal-integrated score achieved AUC of 0.94, 0.88 and 0.84 in the training, internal validation and external validation datasets, respectively. For high pathological burden, the AUCs were 0.92, 0.80, and 0.77. In the outcome dataset, the score was an independent predictor of early recurrence (HR = 2.71; p = 0.004) and improved prognostic discrimination when combined with pathologic predictors. Conclusion This CT-based score, integrating fractal biomarkers, enables accurate, noninvasive preoperative prediction of aggressive pathological features in PDAC and provides incremental value for early recurrence risk stratification. Key points Question Can the fractal-based imaging features be used to predict high-risk pathological features and guide risk stratification for early recurrence in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC)? Findings This CT-based score integrating fractal analysis predicted high-risk pathological features and was independent predictors of early recurrence and provided incremental prognostic value beyond pathologic factors. Clinical relevance This CT-based imaging score may help identify patients at high-risk of aggressive pathology before surgery and may further complement postoperative pathological risk stratification for early recurrence.

title: Virtual liver biopsy for detecting steatohepatitis in chemotherapy-treated patients: comparison with whole-liver radiomics and external validation.
abstract: Objectives Chemotherapy-associated steatohepatitis (CASH) increases the risk of postoperative liver failure and mortality in patients undergoing liver surgery. However, non-invasive diagnosis remains an unmet need. Radiomics has potential for characterizing liver parenchyma. This study evaluated the performance of a virtual liver biopsy for CASH prediction, comparing it with whole-liver radiomic analysis. Materials and methods Two retrospective series of patients undergoing hepatectomy for colorectal liver metastases were analyzed: the public "Colorectal-Liver-Metastases" dataset (training and internal validation) and a monocenter series from Humanitas Research Hospital (external validation). Inclusion criteria were preoperative chemotherapy (≥ 2 months) and post-chemotherapy CT (thickness ≤ 5 mm). IBSI-compliant radiomic features were extracted from whole-liver parenchyma and from a virtual biopsy (manually segmented 2-mL cylinder of non-tumoral liver parenchyma). Estimated liver volume (eLV) was computed using three orthogonal diameters. Four XGBoost models were developed (70/30 split, 5-fold cross-validation): clinical; clinical + VB-radiomics (ViB); clinical + VB-radiomics + eLV (ViBE+); clinical + whole-liver radiomics (WholeLiver). Results One hundred eighty patients were included: 105 internal (63 males, mean age 58.9 years, 38% CASH+) and 75 external (44 males, mean age 62.4 years, 19% CASH+). WholeLiver and ViBE+ models achieved excellent and comparable performance in internal validation (WholeLiver: AUC = 0.857 (95% BS-CI: 0.676-0.954), accuracy = 0.774 (95% BS-CI: 0.613-0.903); ViBE + : AUC = 0.831 (95% BS-CI: 0.549-0.956), accuracy = 0.839 (95% BS-CI: 0.710-0.935); p = 0.814), outperforming ViB model (AUC = 0.724 (95% BS-CI: 0.483-0.896), accuracy = 0.774 (95% BS-CI: 0.613-0.903)). SHAP analysis confirmed liver volume metrics as key predictors. In external validation, the ViBE+ model achieved AUC = 0.745 (95% BS-CI: 0.604-0.886) and accuracy = 0.680 (95% BS-CI: 0.562-0.783). Conclusion Virtual biopsy provides a reproducible, non-invasive radiomic sampling strategy for CASH prediction. Combined with liver volume metrics, it achieves performance comparable to whole-liver analysis, supporting its potential clinical application. Key points Question Despite its association with postoperative morbidity, the non-invasive preoperative assessment of CASH remains challenging in patients undergoing liver surgery. Findings Radiomic analysis based on a virtual liver biopsy, combined with volumetric measurements, showed excellent performance in predicting CASH, comparable to whole-liver analysis, with liver volume emerging as a key predictor. Critical Relevance Statement A standardized virtual biopsy-based radiomic analysis represents a promising non-invasive approach for evaluating liver parenchymal injury, as demonstrated in preoperative assessment of CASH and identification of high-risk surgical patients.

title: TotalSpineSeg: automated whole-spine vertebral segmentation with high robustness to labeling errors.
abstract: Objectives To develop TotalSpineSeg, a robust tool for vertebrae and intervertebral disc instance segmentation, along with spinal cord and spinal canal segmentation, capable of processing any 3D medical image regardless of contrast, resolution, or field of view, while overcoming fusion and fragmentation errors common in standard segmentation. Materials and methods A two-stage cascaded deep learning model was trained on 1404 MRIs. To explicitly prevent errors where adjacent vertebrae merge or a single vertebra splits, the architecture employs a novel "odd/even" representation. The second stage is conditioned on an odd-intervertebral disc mask from the first stage to assign distinct semantic classes to alternating vertebrae, enforcing accurate separation between neighboring vertebrae. Finally, a landmark-based logic uses key anatomical points (C2-C3, C7-T1, T12-L1, and L5-S) to anchor sequential labeling, while a localizer-based strategy ensures accurate identification even in truncated, short field-of-view scans. Results Evaluation across diverse contrasts and pathologies yielded a vertebral identification rate of 96.22% on localizer MRI and generalized to CT scans with a 92.87% identification rate. For intervertebral disc instance labeling, where vertebral separation is not mandatory, both model stages attained 99% labeling accuracy with a mean positional L2 error of 1.55 mm, surpassing existing state-of-the-art methods. Conclusion TotalSpineSeg successfully generalizes to diverse 3D medical images, overcoming variations in contrast, resolution, and field of view. The proposed topological constraints effectively eliminate vertebral fusion and fragmentation errors, delivering a state-of-the-art identification rate for both vertebrae and intervertebral discs across MRI and CT modalities. Key points Question Can a topology-constrained framework overcome heterogeneous contrasts and resolution limits, including localizers, to ensure robust, automated vertebral and disc labeling? Findings TotalSpineSeg achieved a high identification rate across diverse contrasts, localizers, and CT, surpassing state-of-the-art methods by eliminating fusion and fragmentation errors. Clinical relevance TotalSpineSeg enables fully automated biomarker extraction from clinical scans, allowing precise assessment of stenosis, lesions, and atrophy against normative ranges.

title: CT-derived fractional flow reserve for anatomically long-segment coronary disease: a multicentre diagnostic accuracy study.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the diagnostic performance of CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) for detecting haemodynamically significant coronary disease in patients with anatomically long-segment lesions. Materials and methods This retrospective multicentre study included patients who underwent coronary CT angiography and invasive pressure-wire FFR within 30 days. Anatomically long-segment disease was defined as lesion length ≥ 20 mm. Invasive FFR ≤ 0.80 was the reference standard. CT-FFR was assessed at vessel and patient levels, with patient-level CT-FFR defined as the minimum value per patient and patient-level disease as any invasive FFR ≤ 0.80. Diagnostic discrimination, threshold-based classification, and Bland-Altman agreement were evaluated. Results The diagnostic cohort included 329 patients and 377 vessels; 137 patients and 144 vessels had anatomically long-segment disease. At the vessel level, CT-FFR achieved an AUC of 0.941 (95% CI: 0.917-0.966), sensitivity of 94.3%, specificity of 83.7%, and accuracy of 88.6%. In anatomically long-segment vessels, the AUC was 0.961 (95% CI: 0.922-1.000), with sensitivity of 95.7%, specificity of 92.2%, and accuracy of 94.4%. At the patient level, the overall AUC was 0.941 (95% CI: 0.915-0.967) and 0.971 (95% CI: 0.934-1.000) in anatomically long-segment disease. Mean bias was small, although limits of agreement were clinically relevant. Conclusion CT-FFR showed high diagnostic discrimination for invasive FFR-defined ischaemia, including in anatomically long-segment disease. However, agreement limits and threshold-zone uncertainty support its use as a non-invasive physiological adjunct rather than a direct substitute for invasive pressure-wire assessment. Key points Question Does machine learning-based CT-FFR maintain diagnostic performance for invasive FFR-defined ischaemia in anatomically long-segment coronary lesions? Findings CT-derived FFR showed high diagnostic discrimination overall and maintained performance in anatomically long-segment disease, although subgroup comparisons remained exploratory. Clinical relevance CT-derived FFR may provide non-invasive physiological information in anatomically long-segment coronary disease before invasive angiography, while values near the 0.80 threshold require cautious interpretation.

The diagnostic cohort included 329 patients and 377 vessels; 137 patients and 144 vessels had anatomically long-segment disease. At the vessel level, CT-FFR achieved an AUC of 0.941 (95% CI: 0.917-0.966), sensitivity of 94.3%, specificity of 83.7%, and accuracy of 88.6%. In anatomically long-segment vessels, the AUC was 0.961 (95% CI: 0.922-1.000), with sensitivity of 95.7%, specificity of 92.2%, and accuracy of 94.4%. At the patient level, the overall AUC was 0.941 (95% CI: 0.915-0.967) and 0.971 (95% CI: 0.934-1.000) in anatomically long-segment disease. Mean bias was small, although limits of agreement were clinically relevant.

Conclusion

CT-FFR showed high diagnostic discrimination for invasive FFR-defined ischaemia, including in anatomically long-segment disease. However, agreement limits and threshold-zone uncertainty support its use as a non-invasive physiological adjunct rather than a direct substitute for invasive pressure-wire assessment.

Key points

Question Does machine learning-based CT-FFR maintain diagnostic performance for invasive FFR-defined ischaemia in anatomically long-segment coronary lesions? Findings CT-derived FFR showed high diagnostic discrimination overall and maintained performance in anatomically long-segment disease, although subgroup comparisons remained exploratory. Clinical relevance CT-derived FFR may provide non-invasive physiological information in anatomically long-segment coronary disease before invasive angiography, while values near the 0.80 threshold require cautious interpretation.

title: Evaluating strategies to optimize breast MRI screening: a modeling study of abbreviated protocols, dockable tables, and staffing scenarios.
abstract: Objective MRI is increasingly recommended for breast cancer screening, particularly in women with dense breast tissue. However, widespread adoption is constrained by limited capacity and high costs. This study evaluated how optimized MRI screening workflows could address these barriers through three targeted interventions: an abbreviated scan protocol, dockable MRI tables, and expanded technician staffing. Materials and methods A calculation model was developed to compare seven workflow strategies against the current standard care. Strategies included reducing MRI acquisition time from 13 to 6 min, introducing dockable tables with breast coils, adding a third technician, and combinations thereof. Workflow durations and cost inputs were derived from published literature, hospital data, and expert opinion. Primary outcomes were daily screening capacity, cost per screening, annual screening costs, and staffing requirements for a screening volume of 5500 screening examinations per year. Results After evaluating several optimized workflow strategies, we found that reducing MRI acquisition time increased daily screening capacity from 30 to 47 scans, with associated annual savings of €147,505 (8.4%) and a reduction of 1320 technician hours. Combined strategies integrating reduced scan time, additional technicians, and dockable tables increased the daily capacity from 30 to 67 scans and reduced annual costs by up to €160,557 (9.2%) compared with the current workflow. Conclusions Optimizing MRI breast cancer screening workflows with abbreviated scan protocols and dockable tables can substantially increase screening capacity, reduce costs, and technician workload. This would expand access to MRI screening, without requiring additional scanners, potentially providing a solution for (future) capacity problems. Key points Question Which workflow optimization strategies, including abbreviated scan protocols, dockable tables, and additional technicians, offer the greatest capacity and cost benefits for MRI breast cancer screening? Findings Abbreviated scan protocols provide the largest cost savings, while combined workflow changes can substantially increase capacity and still reduce costs. Clinical relevance Optimizing MRI breast cancer screening workflows with abbreviated scans and dockable tables can increase screening capacity and reduce costs and technician workload. This expands access to MRI screening, without requiring additional scanners, potentially providing a solution for capacity problems.

title: Delayed hepatobiliary phase imaging improves bile leak detection on gadoxetate-enhanced MRI.
abstract: Objectives To compare conventional and delayed (≥ 30 min) hepatobiliary-phase (HBP) gadoxetate-enhanced MRI for the detection of bile leaks. Materials and methods This retrospective single-center study included all consecutive gadoxetate-enhanced MRI examinations comprising delayed HBP acquisitions performed for suspected biliary leak over 2 years at a tertiary hepatobiliary referral center. Two abdominal radiologists blinded to clinical records independently assessed leak presence at each timepoint. A composite reference standard incorporating endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography, surgical exploration, percutaneous drainage findings, and multidisciplinary assessment was utilized to assign ground-truth leak status. Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values (PPV, NPV), accuracy, and inter-reader agreement were calculated. Results Thirty-five patients (22 men; median age, 56 years; interquartile range (IQR), 48-65) undergoing 36 examinations were included. The most common indications were liver transplantation (n = 13/35, 37%) and cholecystectomy (n = 11/35, 31%). Conventional and delayed HBP were acquired at a median of 21 and 65 min after injection, respectively. Twenty-two of 36 examinations (61%) were ground-truth positive. Inter-reader agreement was perfect for conventional HBP (κ = 1.00) and excellent for delayed HBP (κ = 0.94; 95% CI 0.84-1.00). Conventional HBP demonstrated 27% sensitivity (95% CI 11-50%), 100% specificity (95% CI 77-100%), and 56% accuracy (95% CI 38-72%). Delayed HBP demonstrated 82% sensitivity (95% CI 60-95%), 100% specificity (95% CI 77-100%), and 89% accuracy (95% CI 74-97%). NPV increased from 47% to 78%. Delayed HBP yielded higher sensitivity and overall accuracy than conventional HBP (p < 0.001, exact McNemar tests). Conclusion Delayed HBP improved bile leak detection without loss of specificity. Key points Question Does extending gadoxetate hepatobiliary-phase MRI acquisitions beyond the conventional 20-min window improve the detection of active bile leaks? Findings Delayed hepatobiliary-phase imaging raised sensitivity for bile leak detection from 27% to 82% without loss of specificity, highlighting acquisition timing as a key diagnostic determinant. Clinical relevance Delayed gadoxetate hepatobiliary-phase imaging is an effective adjunct for detecting active bile leaks and should be considered when findings at conventional timing are negative or equivocal, with direct implications for clinical management.

title: AI for reducing claims and compensation payments from missed fractures on radiographs.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the potential of BoneView, an artificial intelligence (AI) tool for fracture detection on radiographs in claims cases related to missed fractures that resulted in financial compensation. Materials and methods This retrospective, multicenter study included all patients who submitted a claim and received financial compensation for missed fractures on radiographs between January 2013 and December 2019 across the 38 university hospitals of the Greater Paris area (AP-HP-France). For each claimant, 5 control patients were selected from a contemporary single-center cohort of patients who underwent radiographs of the same anatomical regions (with or without fracture) performed in the emergency department of a university hospital, irrespective of fracture status. Three radiologists (musculoskeletal fellow, 5-year fellowship-trained radiologist, and > 20-year expert) independently performed blinded, unassisted, and AI-assisted interpretations following a 3-month washout. Sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were calculated with and without AI and for standalone AI. Compensation amounts were used to estimate potentially avoidable payouts. Results 156 patients (mean age, 42.2 years; 113 (72.4%) males), including 26 claimants with missed fractures on radiographs and 130 controls, were evaluated. 27/130 (20.8%) of the control cohort had fractures. Standalone AI sensitivity was 80.8% (21/26; 95% CI [60.7-93.5]) for claimants and 96.3% (26/27; 95% CI [81.0-99.9]) for the control cohort (p = 0.10). AI assistance did not significantly improve sensitivity, with expert reader sensitivity increasing from 81.1% to 92.5% (p = 0.10). Total compensation was €282,850 (€10,878 per case). AI-assisted detection could have potentially mitigated €265,314, representing a 93.8% theoretical reduction in institutional financial liability. Conclusion AI-assisted fracture detection identified most missed fractures on radiographs leading to compensation and may help reduce medicolegal risk and compensation-related financial burden. Key points Question Can AI-assisted fracture detection identify fractures missed by radiologists on radiographs that led to compensated medicolegal claims and institutional financial liability? Findings Standalone AI detected 21/26 (80.8%) of missed fractures in patients with compensated claims, corresponding to €265,314/€282,850 (93.8%) of total compensation in this cohort. Clinical relevance AI-assisted fracture detection can potentially increase radiologists' diagnostic accuracy and reduce medicolegal risk and compensation-related financial burden. Implementing AI tools in emergency settings may significantly mitigate patient harm and institutional costs associated with missed fractures.

title: Evolving role of cryoablation and cryoneurolysis for interventional pain management.
abstract: Despite advances in pain management, pain remains a major global health challenge in both oncological and non-oncological patients. Long-term pharmacological treatment is often restricted by insufficient therapeutic benefit and adverse events, highlighting the need for alternative approaches such as image-guided pain therapies. The idea of treating pain with cold has been recognized for centuries, and today cryotherapy has emerged as a valuable minimally invasive option for pain management. Cryoablation refers to the destruction of tissue with extreme cold and has an increasing role, especially in the treatment of benign (e.g., osteoid osteoma), malignant bone (i.e., metastases), and soft tissue tumors, either with a curative or palliative intent. Cryoneurolysis is a related but distinct application, focusing either on peripheral nerve modulation or nerve destruction. Cryoneurolysis may be highly effective for the treatment of acute or chronic pain, including sympathetic neurolysis in cancer and non-cancer-related pain syndromes. The general approach in patients with tumor-related pain depends on whether the lesion itself can be ablated or not. In non-oncologic patients, cryoneurolysis of the responsible nerve is typically performed following a positive response to a diagnostic nerve block. Potential indications for cryotherapy are constantly evolving; however, evidence, especially for cryoneurolysis, is still limited and based mostly on single-center case series and retrospective studies. Standardized ablation protocols are lacking, and for the duration of cycles, most experts rely on imaging visualization and validated protocols. Equally important, successful integration of cryoablation and cryoneurolysis into daily practice requires structured workflows across different patient pathways and interdisciplinary management. KEY POINTS: Question Pain management remains a major global health challenge and an unmet need in oncological and non-oncological patients. Findings Cryotherapy, in terms of cryoablation and cryoneurolysis, is increasingly incorporated in multimodal curative and palliative pain care concepts, for treatment of acute and chronic pain syndromes. Clinical relevance Advancement and validation of standardized treatment protocols are needed to strengthen evidence and further enhance clinical implementation in interventional radiology practice and interdisciplinary patient care.

title: Commercially available AI medical devices for prostate MRI: current evidence and opportunities for implementation.
abstract: Objective Artificial intelligence (AI) may improve prostate MRI interpretation and reduce radiologist workload, but evidence supporting clinical implementation remains limited. This scoping review summarises evidence on commercially available AI medical devices for prostate MRI. Materials and methods PubMed was searched for studies published through October 1, 2026. Eligible devices were cleared by the United States Food and Drug Administration and/or CE marked, with commercial availability corroborated through manufacturer websites. Data extraction addressed standalone AI performance, AI-assisted radiologist performance, workflow efficiency, and downstream clinical impact. Results Twenty-one studies evaluating 7 commercial AI systems were included; 17/21 (81%) were retrospective and 14/21 (67%) were single-centre. AI assistance suggested greater benefit for less-experienced readers, but improvements were inconsistent and increased specificity sometimes accompanied reduced sensitivity. Standalone evaluations, outside the devices' approved intended use, showed discrimination comparable to that of radiologists in selected cohorts. Inter-reader agreement and workflow benefits were mixed. We identify three key limitations of the current body of evidence that require thoughtful consideration before routine implementation: (1) incomplete verification strategies, (2) limited determination of workflow benefit, and (3) lack of analyses of cost-effectiveness and patient outcomes, e.g., time to treat or cancer-free survival. Conclusion Evidence supporting the use of commercial AI for prostate MRI remains limited and heterogeneous, with inconsistent diagnostic benefits. Prospective comparative studies in real clinical workflows are needed to determine its potential role within the prostate cancer diagnostic pathway. Key points Question Evidence for clinical implementation of prostate AI remains limited-most studies are retrospective and single-centre, with heterogeneous populations and reference standards. Findings AI may improve diagnostic performance for less-experienced readers, but gains for expert readers and assessment of workflow efficiency are limited. Clinical relevance Prospective multicentre studies embedded in real-world pathways are needed, together with analyses of cost-effectiveness and patient outcomes.

Findings AI may improve diagnostic performance for less-experienced readers, but gains for expert readers and assessment of workflow efficiency are limited. Clinical relevance Prospective multicentre studies embedded in real-world pathways are needed, together with analyses of cost-effectiveness and patient outcomes.

title: Systolic pressure gradient across myocardial bridge mediates the effect of bridge depth on clinical symptoms.
abstract: Objective The relationship between myocardial bridging (MB) morphology and function and the pathways to clinical symptoms remained unclear. This study investigated the association between delta coronary computed tomographic angiography-derived fractional flow reserve (ΔCT-FFR) and angina-equivalent symptoms in left anterior descending MB without coronary atherosclerosis using photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT). Materials and methods This retrospective cohort included 180 patients with deep MB (depth > 2 mm) and no plaques. All underwent PCD-CT angiography. CT-FFR was computed by machine learning; systolic (ΔCT-FFRsys) and diastolic (ΔCT-FFRdia) trans-bridge pressure gradients were derived. MB depth and length were measured. Associations with symptoms were assessed by logistic regression and mediation analysis. Results Symptomatic patients (n = 81) had greater depth (median 3.30 mm vs. 2.45 mm), longer length (mean 36.06 mm vs. 26.10 mm), higher ΔCT-FFRsys (3.81% vs. 1.62%) and ΔCT-FFRdia (3.45% vs. 2.15%) than asymptomatic patients (n = 99) (all p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis identified depth (OR = 1.77, 95% CI: 1.27-2.46, p = 0.001) and ΔCT-FFRsys (OR = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.05-1.27, p = 0.002) as independent predictors. Mediation analysis indicated that ΔCT-FFRsys significantly mediated the effect of depth on symptoms (indirect effect = 0.1881, 95% CI: 0.1023-0.2897). Conclusions MB depth and ΔCT-FFRsys were independent risk factors for symptoms, and ΔCT-FFRsys appeared to mediate the morphological-clinical symptoms link. These findings suggested that integrated assessment, particularly ΔCT-FFRsys, might be a new non-invasive imaging biomarker for clinically identify symptomatic MB and understand its potential pathogenic mechanisms. Key points Question The precise relationship between myocardial bridging morphological and functional features and clinical symptoms, and whether underlying key mediating factors exist, remains currently incompletely determined. Findings Depth, length, and systolic trans-bridge pressure gradient of myocardial bridging independently predicted symptoms, with the gradient significantly mediating the relationship between morphology and clinical presentation. Clinical relevance Noninvasive assessment of depth and systolic trans-bridge pressure gradient can assist in identifying patients with symptomatic myocardial bridging, serving as potential imaging biomarkers and providing insights into the underlying pathophysiology of symptom presentation.

title: Improved detection of central vein sign in multiple sclerosis using optimized susceptibility weighted imaging at 3 Tesla.
abstract: Objectives The central vein sign (CVS) is a novel diagnostic imaging biomarker that improves differentiation of white matter lesions (WMLs) caused by multiple sclerosis (MS) and radiological mimics. While susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) is widely available for visualizing venous structures, standard SWI protocols are not optimized for standalone CVS detection and require T2-FLAIR images to co-localize T2-hyperintense WMLs. This study evaluated whether an optimized SWI protocol improves CVS detection and reader confidence at 3 T. Materials and methods Seventeen patients with a clinical diagnosis of MS were scanned on a 3 T MRI scanner using a standard SWI and an optimized SWI acquired with a lower flip angle (FA = 5°). Two radiologists, blinded to the SWI imaging protocols, evaluated the presence of CVS and their confidence levels. Subsequent subject-level analysis was performed to assess the positive detection rate for MS using the "Select-6" rule. Results Optimized SWI detected all CVS+ lesions identified by standard SWI plus 33 additional lesions (105 vs. 72). Optimized SWI detected more CVS+ lesions than standard SWI in 14/17 participants, with a higher median number of CVS+ lesions detected per participant (7.0 vs. 4.0; p < 0.001). Optimized SWI also increased high-confidence CVS+ classification compared with standard SWI (p = 0.006). Positive detection rate for MS using Select-6 increased from 41.2% with standard SWI to 82.4% with optimized SWI (p = 0.016). Conclusion This feasibility study demonstrates that acquiring SWI with a lower FA at 3 T significantly improves CVS detection, reader confidence, and positive detection rate for MS. Key points Question Standard SWI can visualize venous structures at 3 T, but provides limited lesion conspicuity, which prevents standalone detection of the central vein sign (CVS). Findings Optimized SWI with a low flip angle detects more CVS-positive lesions, increases high-confidence CVS classification, and improves MS detection rate using the Select-6 rule. Clinical relevance Optimized SWI improves CVS visibility and rater confidence without increasing scan time, providing a simple technical optimization for assessment of CVS at 3 T.

title: Ultrasound quantification of liver fat in MASLD.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent and frequently first recognized at ultrasound, but conventional B-mode assessment is limited by subjectivity and reduced sensitivity for mild steatosis. Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) techniques address these limitations by converting acoustic signal properties into numerical biomarkers of hepatic fat, including attenuation coefficient, backscatter coefficient, speed of sound, and composite measures. This review summarizes the technical principles, current evidence, clinical implementation, and limitations of ultrasound-based liver fat quantification techniques in MASLD. Their major advantages are accessibility, integration into routine ultrasound examinations, and potential use alongside elastography for multiparametric assessment. However, thresholds vary across vendors, software implementations, acquisition protocols, reference standards, and patient populations, limiting interchangeability and universal cutoffs. In clinical practice, ultrasound fat quantification should not be interpreted in isolation but integrated with fibrosis risk stratification and metabolic risk assessment. Further multicenter studies are needed to standardize acquisition and reporting, define clinically meaningful longitudinal changes, and link ultrasound-derived fat reduction with patient outcomes. QUS is therefore best regarded as an evolving, practical framework for objective steatosis assessment that complements, rather than replaces, comprehensive MASLD risk stratification. KEY POINTS: Question Conventional B-mode ultrasound is subjective and insensitive to mild hepatic steatosis, creating an unmet need for objective, reproducible liver fat quantification in MASLD. Findings Attenuation-based and composite quantitative ultrasound methods provide objective liver fat assessment, but vendor-dependent thresholds currently limit interchangeability and universal clinical application. Clinical relevance Quantitative ultrasound enables accessible, objective liver fat assessment during routine imaging, improving detection and grading of hepatic steatosis and supporting risk-based MASLD care; however, vendor-specific thresholds and acquisition variability require technique-specific interpretation.

title: Detection of recurrence after surgical treatment for urachal adenocarcinoma: diagnostic yield of cystoscopy, imaging and serum tumor markers.
abstract: Purpose Recurrence after surgical treatment of urachal adenocarcinoma (UrAC) occurs in up to 60% of patients, yet evidence-based surveillance strategies are lacking. We evaluated, which diagnostic modality first detected local and distant recurrence after surgery for UrAC and determined their yield to inform evidence-based follow-up. Methods We identified 65 consecutive patients from our prospectively maintained database (1994-2022) who were surgically treated with partial or total cystectomy. Routine follow-up up to 10 years consisted of cystoscopy, serum tumor-markers (STMs - CEA and/or CA19-9) and CT-scan according to our institutional protocol. Diagnostic yield was calculated as the number of recurrences detected until first recurrence divided by the number of examinations performed. Results Of the 65 patients, 33 (51%) developed a recurrence. Isolated local recurrence occurred in four patients (6%), while 29 patients (45%) developed distant recurrence. Recurrence was first detected by symptoms in 39% of patients and by routine follow-up in 61%. Routine cystoscopy detected local recurrence in 2 of 304 examinations; Both patients had simultaneous distant recurrence. For distant recurrence, CT and STMs detected recurrence first in 38%(11/29) and in 28%(8/29) patients, respectively. Conclusion Recurrence after surgery for UrAC is common and predominantly distant. Cross-sectional imaging and STMs contribute most to recurrence detection, whereas routine cystoscopic surveillance rarely detected isolated local recurrence.

title: Super-pulsed thulium fiber laser-assisted retrograde intrarenal surgery is a viable alternative to supine and prone percutaneous nephrolithotomy for solitary 20-30 mm renal stones: clinical outcomes, efficacy, and safety analysis.
abstract: Objective Percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) is currently considered the standard treatment for renal stones measuring 20-30 mm. However, recent advances in thulium fiber laser (TFL) technology have expanded the role of retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS) in the management of larger stone burdens. This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of super-pulsed thulium fiber laser (SP-TFL)-assisted RIRS, supine PCNL (BS-PCNL), and prone PCNL (P-PCNL) for the treatment of solitary renal stones measuring 20-30 mm. Materials and methods This retrospective study included patients who underwent surgical treatment for solitary renal stones measuring 20-30 mm at our institution between January 2020 and March 2026. A total of 260 patients were included: 65 underwent BS-PCNL, 117 underwent prone PCNL, and 78 underwent SP-TFL-assisted RIRS. The primary outcome was the stone-free rate, assessed by low-dose computed tomography (CT) one month after surgery. Secondary outcomes included operative time, hemoglobin decrease, length of hospital stay, and perioperative complications. Results Baseline demographic and stone-related characteristics were comparable among the three groups. Operative time was significantly longer in the prone PCNL group (92.4 ± 22.7 min; p < 0.001). The first postoperative day stone-free rates were 87.6%, 92.3%, and 78.2% in the BS-PCNL, prone PCNL, and RIRS groups, respectively (p = 0.016). However, no significant difference was observed in the final stone-free rates on the one-month CT evaluation (92.3%, 93.2%, and 89.7%, respectively; p = 0.686). Hemoglobin decrease was significantly lower in the RIRS group (3.2 ± 2.8, 2.9 ± 2.6, and 0.5 ± 0.4 g/dL; p < 0.001). Patients who underwent RIRS also had a shorter hospital stay (1.44 ± 0.77, 1.36 ± 0.68, and 1.12 ± 0.49 days; p = 0.008). Intraoperative and postoperative complication rates were comparable across the three groups. Conclusion SP-TFL-assisted RIRS represents a safe and effective alternative to PCNL for solitary renal stones measuring 20-30 mm. Although early postoperative stone-free rates were lower than those achieved with PCNL, comparable one-month stone-free rates, lower blood loss, and shorter hospitalization suggest that SP-TFL-assisted RIRS may represent an effective alternative to PCNL in appropriately selected patients.

title: Too good to be true? AI performance in CT-based urinary stone detection and classification: EAU endourology systematic review and diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate pooled performance of artificial intelligence (AI) in computed tomography (CT)-based urinary stone detection and classification and identify methodological factors influencing results. Methods This review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261319940). A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar was conducted up to March 15, 2026. Studies evaluating AI-based detection or classification of urolithiasis on CT with available validation/test cohort data (sensitivity/specificity or 2 × 2 tables) were included. A bivariate random-effects model generated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) curves. Meta-regression explored moderators related to dataset composition and AI pipelines. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-AI. Results 14 studies (five detection-based, nine classification-based) were included. Overall pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.967 and 0.979 (AUC 0.987). Classification studies demonstrated higher pooled sensitivity (0.977) and specificity (0.990) compared with detection studies (0.935 and 0.919; AUC 0.945). Significant heterogeneity was observed and influenced by training sample size, class imbalance, presence of bladder stones or other pathologies, and architectural choices. Most studies had high risk of bias, lacked external validation, and frequently used slice-level or pre-selected datasets, potentially overestimating performance. Conclusion Substantial methodological heterogeneity and high risk of bias limit clinical generalizability. Detection studies better reflect real-world workflows and show lower performance. Current evidence does not support routine clinical implementation without standardized reporting and robust external validation.

Purpose

14 studies (five detection-based, nine classification-based) were included. Overall pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.967 and 0.979 (AUC 0.987). title: Non-transecting posteriorly augmented anastomotic ureteroplasty with lingual mucosal onlay grafts: 5-year multi-institutional experience in 52 cases.
abstract: Purpose Complex proximal or mid-ureteral strictures remain a reconstructive challenge, especially in patients with complete obstruction. We aimed to evaluate the short- to mid-term feasibility, safety, and efficacy of non-transecting posteriorly augmented anastomotic ureteroplasty with lingual mucosal onlay grafts (ntPAA-LMGU). Methods In this retrospective, multicentre study, we reviewed adults who underwent robot-assisted ntPAA-LMGU at three centres and had at least 6 months of follow-up. Primary surgical success required the absence of symptoms, the absence of radiographic evidence of recurrent stricture, and freedom from secondary intervention. Renal functional outcomes were assessed by changes in overall estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and serial eGFR values were analysed using a linear mixed-effects model. Results The procedure was completed robotically in all 52 patients. Ten patients (19%) had previously undergone ureteral reconstruction. Median stricture length was 3.0 cm (IQR 2.9), median graft length was 3.0 cm (IQR 2.0), and median graft width was 1.5 cm (IQR 0.3). Median operative time was 167 min (IQR 75), median estimated blood loss was 50 mL (IQR 30), and median postoperative hospital stay was 6 days (IQR 2). No open conversion or intraoperative complications occurred. At a median follow-up of 17 months (IQR 13), the renal functional success rate was 94% (49/52), and the surgical success rate was 94% (49/52). Postoperative complications occurred in six (12%) patients, including two Clavien-Dindo grade IIIa events. Conclusions ntPAA-LMGU is a safe, feasible, and effective reconstructive option for complex proximal or mid-ureteral strictures.

title: Molecular diagnostics and liquid biopsy approaches in diffuse midline glioma: an update and literature review.
abstract: Purpose Diffuse midline gliomas (DMGs), H3 K27-altered, are aggressive childhood central nervous system tumors that remain almost uniformly fatal. Historically diagnosed radiographically as diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG), these tumors are now defined by integrated anatomic and molecular criteria encompassing H3 K27-mutant, EZHIP-overexpressing, and EGFR-altered subtypes. Advances in tissue sampling have transformed understanding of their molecular landscape, but their eloquent location, the sampling bias inherent to stereotactic biopsy, and the impracticality of repeated tissue sampling have motivated interest in biofluid-based approaches. Liquid biopsy is being investigated as a complementary modality for molecular characterization, longitudinal monitoring, and detection of progression and resistance. Methods A narrative review of the literature was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE for articles published through 31 July 2026, supplemented by a ClinicalTrials.gov search performed on the same date. Eligible articles described liquid biopsy methodologies, biomarker substrates, or clinical applications in DMG or DIPG; a separate, explicitly labeled category of enabling or methodologically relevant studies performed on tissue or in other tumor types was retained. Results We summarize the WHO CNS5 molecular definition of DMG, the role and limitations of tissue-based diagnosis, the spectrum of liquid biopsy substrates and platforms with study-level performance data, and the incorporation of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) sampling into interventional DMG trials. We distinguish exploratory biomarker collection from analytically or clinically validated testing, and we address CSF access, safety, selection bias, and turnaround time. Conclusions Liquid biopsy in DMG remains investigational. No application, whether molecular diagnosis, response monitoring, pseudoprogression adjudication, or treatment adaptation, is currently prospectively validated for clinical decision-making. Standardized, prospective, multi-institutional studies with predefined thresholds are required.

title: Intraoperative non-contact three-dimensional measurement of the facial recess using a 4K3D exoscope during cochlear implantation.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the technical feasibility of 4K3D exoscope-based non-contact three-dimensional measurement of the facial recess and explore agreement with scale-calibrated two-dimensional ImageJ measurements in cadaveric specimens and preoperative CT measurements in patients undergoing cochlear implantation. Methods The system used in this study combined an AINNOVI-100 exoscope with SurgeReal 3D Studio. Cadaveric feasibility assessment and method comparison included 10 temporal bones from eight formalin-fixed cadaveric heads. Three-dimensional measurements were compared with scale-calibrated two-dimensional ImageJ measurements. The prospective single-center cohort included 23 patients undergoing cochlear implantation. Intraoperative measurements were compared with preoperative high-resolution computed tomography measurements for exploratory agreement using absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis. Results Cadaveric intraclass correlation coefficients ranged from 0.878 to 0.934. Mean model-generation time was 1.97 s, and the recorded workflow from reconstruction initiation to result storage lasted 46.07 s. 31 of 35 cadaveric measurement attempts were successful (88.6%), including 29 initial successes (82.9%); 4 attempts failed (11.4%). In the 23 clinical cases, agreement was strongest for facial recess width (intraclass correlation coefficient, 0.962). Angular limits of agreement were wider but remained within the stated ± 10° comparison margin in both cohorts. Conclusion This study supports the feasibility of obtaining non-contact quantitative measurements of the exposed facial recess using a 4K3D exoscope. The observed agreement, particularly for facial recess width, and the short reconstruction and measurement times support further evaluation of this workflow for intraoperative anatomical documentation. Future studies should establish three-dimensional measurement accuracy and reproducibility and examine how the resulting information contributes to surgical decision-making.

title: Perilymphatic enhancement suggestive of blood-labyrinthine barrier dysfunction in tumor-negative unilateral asymmetric sensorineural hearing loss on 10-minute postcontrast 3D heavily T2-weighted FLAIR MRI.
abstract: Purpose We hypothesized that a subset of patients with tumor-negative, nonacute unilateral asymmetric sensorineural hearing loss (ASNHL) would show occult perilymphatic enhancement suggestive of blood-labyrinthine barrier (BLB) dysfunction on 10-min postcontrast three-dimensional (3D) heavily T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (hvT2-FLAIR) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). This study aimed to determine its detection rate and regional distribution. Methods This retrospective study included 25 adults with nonacute unilateral ASNHL who underwent 3-T inner-ear MRI after post-imaging exclusion of three vestibular schwannomas from 28 clinically eligible patients. Precontrast 3D FLAIR, precontrast 3D hvT2-FLAIR, and 10-min postcontrast 3D hvT2-FLAIR images were visually scored. Expert-reviewed automated segmentation generated regional normalized signal intensity (NSI), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and contrast-enhancement percentage (CEP). Results Postcontrast 3D hvT2-FLAIR showed definite asymmetric perilymphatic enhancement in 15 of 25 patients (60%), significantly exceeding precontrast 3D FLAIR (8%; p < 0.001) and precontrast 3D hvT2-FLAIR (16%; p = 0.002). Inter-reader agreement was nearly perfect (κ = 0.915). The affected ear exhibited higher NSI and CNR in the basal turn and vestibular complex, and CEP was higher only in the basal turn; these findings remained significant after false discovery rate correction. Basal-turn enhancement did not correlate with high-frequency audiometric asymmetry. Conclusion Ten-minute postcontrast 3D hvT2-FLAIR MRI frequently revealed asymmetric perilymphatic enhancement suggestive of BLB dysfunction in tumor-negative, nonacute unilateral ASNHL, particularly within the cochlear basal turn and vestibular complex. This exploratory finding provides additional inner-ear information beyond routine tumor-exclusion MRI and is compatible with altered BLB permeability, although its longitudinal significance remains to be established.

title: The orbito-pterygo-sphenoidal ligament/posterior septal artery complex as a dual-function anatomical reference for transethmoidal sphenoidotomy.
abstract: Introduction The superior turbinate and sphenoid ostium are commonly used landmarks for sphenoidotomy; however, they may be obscured in severe inflammatory conditions such as eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis (ECRS) or affected by anatomical variations. This study evaluated the orbito-pterygo-sphenoidal ligament/posterior septal artery (OPSL/PSA) complex-guided transethmoidal sphenoidotomy (TES) as an anatomy-based approach for sphenoid sinus entry and controlled inferior extension of anterior sphenoid wall (ASW) removal. Methods This retrospective study included patients with ECRS who underwent sphenoidotomy. Outcomes were compared between the OPSL/PSA complex-guided TES group (24 patients, 48 sides) and a conventional group (25 patients, 50 sides). The primary endpoint was postoperative residual inferior ASW height measured using computed tomography. Secondary endpoints included ASW width, intraoperative events, operative time, and postoperative exploratory outcomes. Results Postoperative residual inferior ASW height was significantly smaller in the OPSL/PSA complex-guided TES group than in the conventional group (-0.8 ± 1.8 vs. 1.5 ± 2.5 mm; p < 0.001). The difference remained significant after adjustment for potential confounders. Superior turbinate resection was not performed in the OPSL/PSA complex-guided TES group, whereas it was performed in 28.0% of sides in the conventional group. No statistically significant differences in operative time or PSA-related hemorrhage were observed between groups. Conclusions The OPSL/PSA complex-guided TES was associated with a greater extent of inferior ASW removal and less frequent superior turbinate resection, with no statistically significant differences in operative time or ​PSA-related hemorrhage between groups. The OPSL/PSA complex may serve as a complementary anatomical reference with a dual function: assisting sphenoid sinus entry and guiding controlled inferior ASW removal in patients with ECRS.

title: Sex estimation in a Malaysian population using radiographic measurements of the femur and humerus.
abstract: Sex estimation plays a vital role in forensic anthropology, particularly in the identification of unknown human remains. Thisstudy investigates sexually dimorphic traits in radiographic images for the purpose of estimating biological sex. Specifically, measurements of the femur and humerus were analysed, as these long bones exhibit significant sexual dimorphism. A total of 200 individuals were included in this study. X-ray images of the femur and humerus were obtained from the Department of Radiology, Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM), Malaysia. The dataset included demographic information such as age, sex, and individuals of Malay, Chinese, and Indian population group. Measurements of the epicondylar breadth (EB) and vertical head diameter (VD) of both the femur and humerus were recorded. Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) was applied to evaluate the effectiveness of these measurements for sex estimation. The results demonstrated that the combination of two bone parameters achieved an overall classification accuracy exceeding 85% in sex estimation. These findings highlight significant morphological differences between males and females and provide a statistically robust approach for sex estimation in a Malaysian population.

title: Predictive modeling of sex from proximal femoral morphometry using machine learning algorithms: a radiological study in Egyptian adults.
abstract: Sex estimation is a foundational step in forensic identification, and the proximal femur, whether assessed through direct skeletal measurement or radiographic imaging, has shown considerable promise as a durable, sexually dimorphic anatomical region for this purpose. Machine learning (ML) classifiers offer a flexible alternative to traditional discriminant function analysis, yet Egyptian data combining radiographic proximal femoral morphometry with supervised ML remain limited. Hence, this study aimed to develop and compare ML models for sex estimation from proximal femoral radiographic measurements in an adult Egyptian population. Digital pelvic radiographs of 306 Egyptian adults, 135 males and 171 females, aged ≥ 30 years, were retrospectively analyzed. Four proximal femoral measurements, femoral head diameter, femoral neck axis length, femoral neck width, and intertrochanteric distance, were obtained after confirming bilateral symmetry. Nine supervised algorithms were trained and evaluated using cross-validation together with an independent hold-out test set, with performance assessed through accuracy, F1-score, and receiver operating characteristic analysis. All four measurements differed significantly between sexes, with femoral head diameter showing the largest effect size and emerging as the dominant predictor across most models. The decision tree classifier achieved the highest test-set accuracy at 86% (F1-score = 0.83), followed by the multilayer perceptron at 83% (F1-score = 0.82), although sex-specific accuracy revealed nontrivial classification bias for most models, with only gradient boosting and AdaBoost remaining within the 5% bias threshold generally considered acceptable in forensic practice. Area under the curve values ranged between approximately 0.85 and 0.91 on the test set. These findings suggest that proximal femoral radiographic measurements, and femoral head diameter in particular, may offer a reliable and population-specific basis for ML-assisted sex estimation in Egyptian adults. However, sex-specific performance, not accuracy alone, should guide the choice of any model intended for forensic application.

title: Feasibility of reducing Angiofil ® concentration in multiphase postmortem CT angiography and implications for iodine consumption and environmental sustainability : an observational study.
abstract: Background Postmortem CT angiography (PMCTA) is widely used in forensic medicine to evaluate the vascular system before autopsy. The contrast mixture of 3,500 ml paraffin and 210 ml Angiofil ® , originally proposed by Grabherr et al. for multiphase postmortem CT angiography (MPMCTA) approach, provides reliable global vascular opacification. Recent advances in CT detector technology, image reconstruction techniques, and growing environmental concerns have encouraged the investigation of alternative contrast-agent dilutions aimed to reduce iodine consumption. The aim of this observational study was to explore whether lower Angiofil ® concentrations could be used while preserving adequate vascular visualization and diagnostic image quality. Methods Thirty cases were evaluated using four progressively diluted Angiofil ® -paraffin mixtures containing 200 ml, 180 ml, 150 ml, and 120 ml of Angiofil ® in 3,500 ml of paraffin. Contrast enhancement was quantified by measuring Hounsfield units (HU) within regions of interest (ROIs) placed in the ascending thoracic aorta and compared with a clinical case. Image quality was independently assessed by an experienced forensic radiologist based on opacification of the ascending thoracic aorta. In addition, a dedicated evaluation of coronary artery lumen and wall visualization was performed. Results The mixture containing 200 ml of Angiofil ® showed no relevant improvement in image quality compared with the original dilution. A mixture containing 180 ml of Angiofil ® allowed excellent vascular assessment in individuals with a BMI > 35 kg/m², whereas 150 ml of Angiofil ® provided optimal image quality in individuals with a BMI ≤ 35 kg/m². The 120 ml mixture remained diagnostically acceptable in most cases but produced photon-starvation artifacts in individuals with high muscle mass or a BMI > 33 kg/m², limiting vascular assessment. Conclusion Adjusting the Angiofil ® -paraffin mixture according to body morphology using 180 ml of Angiofil ® for individuals with a BMI > 35 kg/m² and 150 ml for those with a BMI ≤ 35 kg/m² maintains excellent vascular visualization while substantially reducing iodine consumption. This optimization supports more environmentally sustainable PMCTA practice without compromising diagnostic image quality.

title: Semi-automated sex estimation from the cochlea on routine clinical CT: limited incremental value of curvature-based shape descriptors.
abstract: Background Sex estimation is fundamental in forensic anthropology and bioarchaeology, yet classical methods rely on skeletal elements that are often absent or poorly preserved. The bony labyrinth, enclosed within the petrous bone, is a promising alternative owing to its early maturation and taphonomic resistance, and cochlear shape has been reported to carry a sex-specific signal. However, most approaches depend on manual segmentation, micro-CT, or complex shape-analysis frameworks that limit routine applicability. Objective To evaluate the feasibility of a semi-automated method for sex estimation from the cochlea using standard clinical CT and automated OTOPLAN segmentation, and to quantify the contribution of shape descriptors beyond cochlear size alone. Materials and methods We analyzed 139 cochleae from 87 adults using clinical CT scans (slice thickness ≤ 0.6 mm). The three-dimensional lateral wall path was extracted with OTOPLAN; after normalization and resampling, curvature- and torsion-based descriptors and scalar cochlear metrics were computed to train a supervised classifier. Preprocessing, feature, and hyperparameter choices were optimized by Bayesian optimization within a nested cross-validation, so that model selection and performance estimation used separate data. Six feature configurations were compared, with all partitions made at the patient level and the whole procedure repeated over five random partitions. Results In nested cross-validation, the best configurations reached an area under the ROC curve (AUC-ROC) of approximately 0.71. A model using cochlear diameter as its sole predictor did not differ detectably from those combining size and shape descriptors (AUC-ROC 0.71, 95% CI 0.62-0.80) and gave the highest balanced accuracy (0.70), with a sensitivity of 0.71 and a specificity of 0.70. Configurations restricted to shape descriptors reached a median AUC-ROC of 0.59, with lower confidence limits at or just above chance level (0.50-0.51). Adding curvature to diameter changed the median AUC by + 0.011 (95% CI - 0.064 to + 0.107). Conclusion Sex-related information is recoverable from cochlear geometry on routine clinical CT using a semi-automated pipeline, but no incremental value of shape descriptors beyond cochlear size was detected. Although accuracy remains moderate, the approach is non-destructive, scalable, and clinically compatible, offering a potential adjunct for forensic anthropology and bioarchaeology when conventional methods are unavailable. This is not an identification method and is not validated as a stand-alone forensic tool: it was evaluated by internal validation only, on in vivo clinical CT.

Adding curvature to diameter changed the median AUC by + 0.011 (95% CI - 0.064 to + 0.107).

Conclusion

Sex-related information is recoverable from cochlear geometry on routine clinical CT using a semi-automated pipeline, but no incremental value of shape descriptors beyond cochlear size was detected. Although accuracy remains moderate, the approach is non-destructive, scalable, and clinically compatible, offering a potential adjunct for forensic anthropology and bioarchaeology when conventional methods are unavailable. This is not an identification method and is not validated as a stand-alone forensic tool: it was evaluated by internal validation only, on in vivo clinical CT.
