title: Development and technical validation of a standardised CT image preprocessing workflow for reproducible AI for forensic anthropological applications.
abstract: The use of computed tomography (CT scans) images is increasing in forensic anthropology to address ethical, logistical, and preservation challenges related to physical cadaveric collections. However, preparing large volumes of medical images for artificial intelligence (AI) applications remains challenging, particularly in terms of standardisation and data privacy. The aim of this study is to develop an automated preprocessing workflow for CT images to support machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) applications in forensic anthropology research and education. Methodology A Python-based pipeline was designed in three stages: data de-identification and sorting, patient table removal, and bone windowing. A script was developed for de-identification, and a custom U-Net architecture was developed for both patient table removal and bone windowing. The workflow was developed and applied to CT thorax. Model performance was evaluated using standard metrics and compared with ground-truth models. Results DICOM metadata de-identification was performed as part of preprocessing; all predefined identifying attributes were successfully processed in the 200 DICOM files examined. The patient table removal model removed the table successfully in 96% of datasets (192/200) and achieved 99.94% accuracy on the original, non-augmented test images. The bone segmentation model achieved a Dice score of 93.12% and a precision of approximately 90%. The segmented 3D models showed high agreement with the ground-truth model, with minimal geometric deviation. Conclusions We have proposed an integrated workflow that provides an ethical, efficient and standardised solution for de-identifying and preprocessing CT imaging data. It also enables the preprocessing of a scalable dataset for AI applications, thereby supporting the development of methodologies for the modern population, with future expansion to full-body scans and other imaging modalities.

title: Post-mortem CT angiography for fatal vascular lesions in forensic death investigation: a systematic review of diagnostic performance, added value, and pitfalls.
abstract: Purpose Post-mortem CT angiography (PMCTA) is increasingly used in forensic death investigation to assess vascular disease, haemorrhage, and traumatic or natural vascular causes of death. However, its practical value depends on the lesion being investigated, the angiographic protocol, and the way imaging findings are integrated with autopsy and pathology. This systematic review evaluated the diagnostic performance, added value, and main pitfalls of PMCTA for fatal vascular lesions. Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane/CENTRAL were searched for human post-mortem studies evaluating PMCTA in forensic, medico-legal, coronial, or post-mortem settings. Eligible studies compared PMCTA with autopsy, histopathology, targeted vascular dissection, or autopsy-based consensus. Evidence was grouped according to practical forensic use, including coronary stenosis assessment, autopsy triage, global vascular lesion detection, haemorrhage-source localization, aortic or traumatic vascular injury assessment, coronary plaque characterization, and artifact-related pitfalls. Risk of bias was assessed using a QUADAS-2-based approach adapted to forensic PMCTA studies. Results The available evidence did not support unrestricted pooling of all fatal vascular lesions. PMCTA was used for different forensic questions, and only coronary stenosis provided data close to conventional diagnostic accuracy assessment. In this domain, available studies showed high specificity but only moderate sensitivity for critical stenosis. Autopsy-triage studies suggested that PMCTA may reduce or guide invasive autopsy in selected adult coronial workflows. Global comparison studies showed added value for vascular lesion detection, and haemorrhage-source studies suggested that PMCTA may help localize bleeding vessels. Evidence on fatal coronary plaque characterization is emerging. Pitfall studies showed that post-mortem clots, incomplete vascular filling, contrast leakage, and extravasation artifacts may mimic or obscure vascular pathology. Conclusion PMCTA is best interpreted as a complementary tool in forensic vascular death investigation rather than as a general substitute for autopsy. Its contribution is strongest when it answers a specific vascular question, such as documenting coronary stenosis, guiding autopsy, mapping vascular lesions, localizing haemorrhage, or supporting targeted histopathology. Careful correlation with autopsy, pathology, case circumstances, and protocol-related artifacts remains essential.

title: Automated whole-dentition CBCT phenotyping enables explainable sex classification and age estimation through distinct dental features.
abstract: Tooth size and morphology are established primarily during development, whereas secondary dentin deposition and pulp-space remodeling continue throughout adulthood, providing biologically distinct information for sex and age estimation. This study investigated whether automated whole-dentition cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) analysis could capture these two signals. The initial cohort comprised 327 adult CBCT scans, of which 275 passed automated segmentation-completeness screening and entered the final analysis (141 female and 134 male participants; age range, 21-61 years). ToothSeg was used for automatic tooth segmentation and numbering. After excluding variables potentially reflecting image acquisition rather than dental biology, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) models were developed separately for sex classification and age regression. Performance was assessed using five-fold out-of-fold predictions, and feature importance was interpreted using SHAP. The sex model achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.807 and an AUC of 0.872, while the age model achieved a mean absolute error of 5.29 years and an R² of 0.645. Lower-right canine volume was the most important individual feature for sex classification and was greater in males (Cohen's d = 1.20). Mean incisor relative low-gray voxel fraction was the most important age feature and was inversely correlated with chronological age (Spearman ρ = -0.706). As an exploratory study, automated whole-dentition CBCT phenotyping showed internally predictive, biologically interpretable patterns for adult sex and age estimation. However, given the modest sample size and proxy low-gray metric, multicenter external and anatomical validation are required.

title: In vivo assessment of brain microstructure in patients with Huntington's disease using quantitative MRI.
abstract: Objectives Using multiparametric mapping (MPM), we assessed the integrity of cortical and subcortical regions across different stages of Huntington's disease (HD), relating the derived findings to genetic modifiers and clinical measures. Methods Sixteen premanifest patients with HD (PwHD pre ), ten manifesting PwHD (PwHD man ), and forty-two healthy controls (HC) underwent clinical examinations and a 3 T imaging. We derived quantitative MPM maps to perform voxel-based quantification (VBQ) and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). We assessed group differences by combining PwHD pre and PwHD man (PwHD total ) and by comparing PwHD pre and PwHD man with age- and sex-matched HC. Using correlation analysis, we investigated the link between MPM-derived findings, CAG repeat length, and clinical scores. Results PwHD man presented with reductions in all four quantitative MPM maps across the bilateral caudate nucleus and the frontal, parietal, temporal, and occipital gyri. We observed spatial overlap between VBQ- and VBM-derived findings, demonstrating widespread volume loss in PwHD man . PwHD pre showed reductions in certain quantitative maps within the frontal and temporal regions. Reduced MPM values correlated with clinical scores of HD severity. Interpretation The observed reductions across four MPM modalities in PwHD man are consistent with demyelination and neuronal loss, as supported by widespread volume loss. The reductions observed in PwHD pre indicate early demyelination and inflammation. In this study, we demonstrated the utility and clinical relevance of MPM for detecting microstructural alterations across different stages of HD. MPM can serve as a non-invasive biomarker of neurodegeneration in HD, providing insight into the pathological events underlying the observed neuronal loss.

title: Thirteen-month real-world effectiveness and safety of lecanemab in Chinese patients with Alzheimer's disease: integrating objective clinical outcomes and caregiver-reported experiences.
abstract: Background The longer-term real-world effectiveness of lecanemab and predictors of treatment response remain unclear in Chinese patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD). Methods This prospective multicenter cohort enrolled patients receiving lecanemab (10 mg/kg biweekly) across nine medical centers in Southwest China. Longitudinal cognition, 13-month amyloid-β positron emission tomography/computed tomography (Aβ-PET/CT), safety, treatment discontinuation, and caregiver-reported Clinical Global Impression (CGI) outcomes were assessed. Cognitive trajectories were compared with propensity score-matched local controls and an external Alzheimer's disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) natural-history cohort. Results Among 122 lecanemab-treated patients, 38.52% had mild cognitive impairment due to AD and 40.98% had mild AD dementia. Linear mixed-effects models incorporating 222 follow-up visits demonstrated generally stable cognitive performance, with modest favorable changes in cognitive scores at certain follow-up time points. At 13 months, 84.00% maintained or improved Clinical Dementia Rating stage, and 66.67% achieved amyloid-negative conversion, defined as a Centiloid value < 12. Lecanemab-treated patients showed more favorable longitudinal cognitive trajectories than matched ADNI and local natural-history controls. Amyloid reduction was not robustly associated with cognitive improvement, and routine baseline clinical variables did not reliably predict treatment response. CGI assessments indicated clinical improvement or stability in 77.55% of participants. Amyloid-related imaging abnormalities and infusion-related reactions occurred in 10.66% and 5.74% of patients, respectively, while treatment discontinuation was most commonly driven by the inconvenience of repeated infusions rather than safety concerns. Conclusion Lecanemab was associated with favorable longitudinal cognitive trajectories, substantial amyloid clearance, and acceptable safety in Chinese patients with AD. However, amyloid reduction and routine baseline clinical characteristics did not reliably predict treatment response.

title: Comparative evaluation of GPT 5.2 Pro and Gemini 3 Pro large multimodal models for retinal optical coherence tomography interpretation.
abstract: Purpose Large multimodal models (LMMs) capable of interpreting medical images are increasingly accessible to patients, yet their reliability for retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) interpretation remains uncertain. This study evaluated the performance of two state-of-the-art LMMs in detecting OCT features and generating diagnostic interpretations. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 330 publicly available retinal OCT B-scans spanning 12 diagnostic categories, including normal scans and common retinal diseases, were analyzed. Two commercially available LMMs (GPT 5.2 Pro and Gemini 3 Pro) were evaluated using zero-shot inference. Models were assessed separately for detection of nine predefined OCT features and for free-text diagnostic interpretation. Feature detection performance was measured using per-feature metrics and macro-averaged F1 scores, while diagnostic accuracy was assessed against expert-adjudicated reference standards. Results Gemini 3 Pro demonstrated higher feature detection performance than GPT 5.2 Pro (macro-averaged F1 score 0.558 vs. 0.472) and higher diagnostic accuracy (58.8% vs. 32.1%). Both models performed better for visually salient abnormalities but showed limited sensitivity for subtle structural features. Normal OCT scans were frequently misclassified as pathological, particularly by GPT 5.2 Pro, which failed to correctly identify any normal images. Recurrent, model-specific diagnostic biases and hallucinated diagnoses were observed. Conclusions Although LMMs can extract clinically relevant information from OCT scans, their diagnostic reliability remains limited, with frequent overcalling of pathology and systematic biases. Given their increasing availability to patients, these limitations raise concerns about potential misinterpretation outside supervised clinical settings. Careful validation and clear usage boundaries are needed before such tools can be safely integrated into patient-facing workflows.

title: The integral role of artificial intelligence models in retinal detachment diagnostics: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Purpose Retinal detachment (RD) is a vision-threatening condition requiring prompt diagnosis and management to optimize visual outcomes. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models have demonstrated promising results in RD detection across multiple imaging modalities; however, concerns regarding heterogeneity, external validation, and real-world implementation remain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance and clinical applicability of AI models for RD diagnostics. Methods A comprehensive electronic search of PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP), and Google Scholar was conducted in April 2026. Studies evaluating ML or DL models for RD detection, classification, segmentation, screening, or prognostic assessment using any imaging modality were included. Two independent reviewers performed study screening, data extraction, and quality assessment using the QUADAS-2 and CLAIM tools. Quantitative syntheses were performed using a bivariate random-effects model to pool sensitivity and specificity, while a random-effects inverse-variance model was applied for diagnostic odds ratio (DOR). Subgroup analyses were conducted according to imaging modality and use of external validation status. Publication bias and small-study effects were assessed using Deeks' funnel plot asymmetry test. Results Sixty-six studies were included in the systematic review, of which 31 studies comprising 118,432 images were eligible for meta-analysis. Fundus photography was the most commonly used imaging modality, and DL approaches predominated. The pooled sensitivity was 0.93 (95% CI: 0.89-0.95) and specificity was 0.98 (95% CI: 0.96-0.99), with moderate between-study heterogeneity. The model-based positive predictive value (PPV) and negative predictive value (NPV) were 0.86 (95% CI: 0.71-0.94) and 0.99 (95% CI: 0.97-1.00), respectively. The SROC curve yielded an AUC of 0.982 and a normalized pAUC of 0.964, while the pooled DOR was 642.3 (95% CI: 264.5-1559.7). No significant publication bias or small-study effects were detected (P = 0.544). Conclusions This study provides the most up-to-date comprehensive quantitative synthesis of AI applications for RD diagnostics, demonstrating excellent overall diagnostic performance across multiple imaging modalities. Despite these promising results, limited external and real-world clinical validation, together with methodological heterogeneity, continue to restrict clinical translation. Future multicenter prospective studies with standardized validation and reporting frameworks are essential for safe and generalizable implementation of AI-assisted RD diagnostics.

title: Neuroendocrine neoplasms of the digestive system: challenges of biopsy diagnosis.
abstract: The diagnosis of digestive neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) is increasingly being made on endoscopic biopsies and endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration/biopsy (EUS-FNA/FNB) or ultrasound biopsies taken from metastases. Although current classification systems provide a robust and elaborate framework for categorizing NENs, their application to limited tissue biopsy samples often remains challenging. A major challenge is the accurate distinction between well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) and poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs), which is essential because of their markedly different prognostic and therapeutic implications. Additional challenges include reliable Ki-67 assessment, recognition of intratumoral heterogeneity, and identification of mixed neoplasms, including mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNENs) and amphicrine-like carcinoma (ALC)-a recently introduced and still poorly characterized category-and assignment of the primary site in metastatic disease using organ-associated immunohistochemical markers. Site-specific differences in morphology and immunophenotype further complicate biopsy interpretation and require integration of histological, immunohistochemical, clinical, and radiological findings. Although morphology remains the cornerstone of diagnosis, molecular testing is increasingly used in difficult cases to identify predictive biomarkers and potentially actionable genomic alterations. This review focuses on a practical biopsy-oriented diagnostic approach, discusses major diagnostic pitfalls, controversial and emerging concepts, and highlights the clinicopathological features of NENs across the digestive tract.

title: A multi-subject tractography atlas of human cerebellar connections.
abstract: The cerebellum is a highly interconnected structure involved in motor coordination and balance as well as cognitive, sensory, autonomic, and emotional functions. Its connectivity relies on complex afferent and efferent white matter pathways linking it with the brainstem, spinal cord, thalamus, cerebral cortex, vestibular system, and limbic-related structures. Recent advances in diffusion MRI (dMRI) and tractography have enabled the in vivo reconstruction of these pathways, offering new opportunities to study cerebellar anatomy and connectivity. However, compared with supratentorial white matter, cerebellar connections remain underexplored owing to their smaller size, anatomical complexity, and the absence of comprehensive tractography atlases. We propose a white matter tractography atlas of candidate cerebellar white matter pathways, consistent with previously reported neuroanatomical descriptions based on regions of interest (ROIs) derived from 30 young healthy volunteers from the Human Connectome Project (HCP). A total of 22 ROIs were segmented to reconstruct, via tractography, 19 cerebellum-associated tractography components, comprising eight bilateral pathways (16 hemisphere-specific reconstructions), and the three major cerebellar white matter conduits: the superior, middle, and inferior cerebellar peduncles (SCP, MCP, and ICP). The eight bilateral pathways comprise the cerebello-ponto-hypothalamic, parieto-ponto-cerebellar, fronto-ponto-cerebellar, occipito-ponto-cerebellar, contralateral cerebello-thalamo-cortical, dentato-rubro-thalamo-cortical, dorsal spinocerebellar, and periaqueductal gray-cerebellar pathways. The delineation of some anatomical regions, particularly the olivary nucleus and the hypothalamus, presented methodological challenges. Difficulties in reliably reconstructing the olivocerebellar pathway led to its exclusion from the final atlas. Two independent neuroanatomical experts evaluated the 19 atlas tracts using four qualitative criteria, finding good anatomical fidelity with overall mean scores of 3.9 and 3.8 out of 5, respectively. The same reconstruction procedure was then applied to 25 additional HCP participants to evaluate the automatic segmentation of these bundles in unseen participants. The proposed atlas provides a framework for studying putative cerebellar structural connectivity, acknowledging that tractography-derived streamlines represent inferred white matter pathways rather than direct evidence of synaptic connections or axonal trajectories and its relationship with motor and non-motor functions. It enables quantitative tractometry analyses derived from diffusion MRI models and facilitates the integration of multimodal and functional information. This atlas may support future research in neuroscience, neuropsychiatric disorders, and neurosurgical planning by providing a standardized representation of cerebellar white matter pathways.

title: Microstructural alterations of human medial temporal lobe in dementia: volumetric and DTI findings correlate with cell number and neuropathology.
abstract: Volumetric and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) alterations in medial temporal lobe (MTL) regions are consistently reported in Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, their biological basis remains poorly understood. We combined Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) metrics with cellular quantification and neuropathological burden assessment to investigate microstructural substrates underlying MTL imaging alterations in human donors with known cognitive and neuropathological status. Absolute cell numbers were quantified in a cohort of 54 brain donors using the isotropic fractionator, and postmortem MRI was performed on a subset of 18 fixed brain hemispheres. To assess microstructural brain alterations associated with disease progression, in vivo volumetric and DTI metrics were analyzed in 39 cognitively unimpaired controls (CU), 31 individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and 14 patients with clinical AD dementia. In the postmortem cohort, MTL diffusivity metrics showed moderate negative correlations with total cell numbers. Mean, axial, and radial diffusivity positively correlated with Braak stage, whereas fractional anisotropy (FA) correlated negatively with CERAD score, linking diffusion alterations to AD-related pathology. In vivo MTL analyses revealed increased mean, axial, and radial diffusivity, and reduced FA in AD patients compared with both CU and MCI individuals. The MCI group exhibited intermediate alterations in diffusivity. Differences between in vivo and postmortem diffusion values were consistent with tissue fixation, temperature, and variations in acquisition protocols. Our findings suggest that diffusion MRI alterations in the MTL are associated with reduced cellularity and neuropathological burden, supporting the biological relevance of DTI metrics as markers of microstructural degeneration in AD.

title: The unfolding symphony: unraveling brain dynamics via data-driven multi-scale functional connectivity in task-state fMRI.
abstract: Task-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) can characterize both regional responses and changes in statistical dependence among distributed brain systems. This narrative review examines dynamic and multiscale connectivity within a broader framework that distinguishes task-modulated functional connectivity, trial-wise covariation, effective connectivity, and data-driven state analysis. Sliding-window correlation, hidden Markov models, and co-activation patterns are compared by their data representations, temporal assumptions, and computational procedures; graph representations can be combined with each of these strategies. We discuss supervised recurrent, transformer, and graph models alongside unsupervised state discovery, self-supervised representation learning, and emerging brain foundation models. Explainability requires evaluation of model attributions, including graph masks and perturbation-based analyses, rather than anatomical plausibility alone. The spatial framework includes whole-brain networks, subnetworks, atlas-defined regions of interest, and voxel- or layer-level measurements. Proposed links across these levels remain hypotheses: faster sampling of the blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) signal does not directly resolve millisecond neural interactions, and resting-state or animal findings do not establish the corresponding mechanism during human tasks. Shared task-evoked responses, hemodynamic variability, motion, and analytical choices can all alter apparent connectivity. Progress therefore depends on matching the estimator to the scientific question, comparing against activation and static-connectivity baselines, and validating results across participants, sessions, and acquisition settings.

title: Associations between peripheral immune markers and brain morphometry in normal individuals.
abstract: Peripheral immune signaling may be associated with brain structure, but evidence in healthy adults remains limited. We conducted a cross-sectional exploratory study to examine associations between circulating immune-marker concentrations and regional cortical morphometry. Structural T1-weighted MRI and peripheral blood samples were obtained from 62 healthcare workers. Cortical volume, surface area, thickness, and mean curvature were extracted for 68 Desikan-Killiany regions using FreeSurfer. Nine peripheral immune markers were measured. Associations were assessed using Spearman rank correlations with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction across 34 regions within each immune-marker, hemisphere, and morphometric-measure family. Associations surviving false discovery rate (FDR) correction in the analyses were further examined using exploratory sensitivity general linear model adjusted for age, sex, and the corresponding global morphometric measure (estimated total intracranial volume for volume and total cortical surface area for surface area). TGF-β1 was the only immune marker with regional associations surviving FDR correction. Higher TGF-β1 concentrations were positively associated with right frontal cortical surface area (Spearman's ρ = 0.367-0.443) and volume (ρ = 0.345-0.502), involving caudal middle frontal, rostral middle frontal, superior frontal, lateral orbitofrontal, and pars orbitalis regions. Exploratory covariate-adjusted sensitivity analyses yielded nominal p-values below 0.05 for right caudal middle frontal surface area (β = 1.609) and volume (β = 4.914), and right superior frontal surface area (β = 2.740) and volume (β = 10.939). No associations involving cortical thickness, mean curvature, or other immune markers survived FDR correction. In this pilot exploratory study of apparently healthy adults, peripheral TGF-β1 concentrations were associated with regional variation in right frontal cortical surface area and volume. These cross-sectional findings do not establish causality, underlying mechanisms, functional relevance, or clinical significance, but provide preliminary hypotheses for larger longitudinal studies of peripheral immune-brain associations.

title: Monitoring of pulmonary outcomes in paediatric cystic fibrosis patients treated with modulator therapy-a narrative review.
abstract: Recently introduced CFTR modulator drugs have transformed the disease trajectories in people with cystic fibrosis. Children with cystic fibrosis, who would once have experienced progressive lung damage and pulmonary function decline from early life onwards, now, when treated with effective modulators, appear to have preserved lung structure and pulmonary function using conventional monitoring tools. However, since cystic fibrosis lung disease may still progress despite effective therapy, early detection of disease manifestation, disease progression, and the tracking of treatment responses remain crucial. Monitoring of lung disease in the current era of CFTR modulators, therefore, poses a fundamental challenge for cystic fibrosis clinicians and researchers. This narrative review summarises currently available monitoring tools for paediatric cystic fibrosis patients. Conclusion In children with cystic fibrosis receiving effective CFTR modulator therapy, spirometry remains an important component of pulmonary monitoring but may be insufficient to detect early or residual lung disease. Complementary approaches, including multiple-breath washout, oscillometry, and structural and functional lung imaging, can provide more sensitive assessment of pulmonary abnormalities and treatment responses. Further development of sensitive, non-invasive biomarkers of airway infection and inflammation, alongside evidence to guide the integration of these tools into routine clinical care, remains an important priority. What is known • CFTR modulator therapy has transformed clinical outcomes in cystic fibrosis, and children initiating effective modulators early in life frequently maintain normal or near-normal pulmonary function. • Conventional monitoring with spirometry, particularly FEV₁, has limited sensitivity for detecting early or residual cystic fibrosis lung disease. What is new • Clinical monitoring of cystic fibrosis lung disease in children has shifted towards the use of technologies allowing for detection of subtle, potentially reversible, structural, functional, and inflammatory abnormalities that may persist despite modulator therapy. • Multiple-breath washout, quantitative computed tomography (CT), functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the chest, as well as emerging biomarkers provide complementary information beyond spirometry and are reshaping contemporary monitoring of CF lung disease.

• Clinical monitoring of cystic fibrosis lung disease in children has shifted towards the use of technologies allowing for detection of subtle, potentially reversible, structural, functional, and inflammatory abnormalities that may persist despite modulator therapy. • Multiple-breath washout, quantitative computed tomography (CT), functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the chest, as well as emerging biomarkers provide complementary information beyond spirometry and are reshaping contemporary monitoring of CF lung disease.

title: Coronary artery calcification is not associated with survival in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer: a secondary analysis of the EXPAND trial.
abstract: Purpose Computed tomography (CT) is the clinical standard for staging of gastrointestinal cancer. Previous studies have highlighted the prognostic significance of coronary artery calcification (CAC) detected by CT in various types of cancer. However, the prognostic role of CAC scoring in gastrointestinal cancers is still unclear. The aim of this study was to investigate the impact of CT-defined CAC on overall survival (OS) in patients with advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer. Methods CAC was semiquantitatively measured using the visual Weston method on baseline CT scans in 785 patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer from the phase III EXPAND trial. This present study is a secondary analysis of the base line CT images. In the original analysis patients were randomly assigned to first-line treatment with cisplatin/capecitabin ± cetuximab. The primary endpoint of the current subanalysis is the OS. For statistical analysis group differences were calculated using the Mann-Whitney-U test and ANOVA test. Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox regression analysis were used to test the effect of CAC on mortality. Results The median CAC score was 1 (IQR 0; 3). A total of 337 patients (42.9%) had no visible CAC (CAC score 0). Male patients had statistically significant higher CAC score compared to female patients (median 1 versus 0, p < 0.0001). In univariable Cox regression CAC showed no significant association with survival when analysed as a continuous value (HR: 0.99, 95% CI: 0.96-1.02, p = 0.74), and when dichotomized for absence and presence of calcification (HR:1.08, 95% CI: 0.92-1.26, p = 0.34). Similar results were identified in further subgroup analyses. Conclusion CT-defined CAC scoring has no relevant prognostic impact in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer undergoing first-line chemotherapy. The present study cannot confirm the promising results for CAC scoring in lung cancer patients.

title: Image quality and dose performance of photon-counting CT in multiple myeloma: a comparative clinical study.
abstract: Purpose To compare image quality and radiation-dose indices between photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) and conventional energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT) examinations in patients with multiple myeloma. Methods This retrospective intraindividual study included 47 patients with non-contrast whole-body PCCT examinations (NAEOTOM Alpha, Siemens Healthineers) and prior EID-CT examinations (SOMATOM Sensation 64, Siemens Healthineers). Examinations were performed using the respective clinical protocols, which differed in acquisition and reconstruction settings. Quantitative image analysis included region-of-interest measurements in the lungs, spleen, muscle, and adipose tissue. Image noise and signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) were calculated. For qualitative assessment, two radiologists independently evaluated randomized and anonymized PCCT and EID-CT scans of the same patients using a 5-point Likert scale to rate overall image quality, sharpness, noise, and osteolytic lesion conspicuity. Qualitative ratings were compared separately for each reader using two-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Differences in CT-dose-index, dose-length-product, and quantitative image metrics were analyzed using two-sided paired t-tests. Results Quantitative analysis demonstrated significantly lower image noise in PCCT compared to EID-CT in the spleen, muscle, and adipose tissue (p < 0.0001), but not in lung tissue (p = 0.27). SNR was significantly higher with PCCT in all tissues except the lungs (p < 0.0001; lungs: p = 0.22; adipose tissue: p = 0.02). Qualitative assessment showed that PCCT was rated significantly better than EID-CT for overall image quality, image sharpness, noise, and osteolysis conspicuity (p < 0.0001 for all categories). Radiation dose parameters (CTDIvol and DLP) were significantly lower with PCCT than with EID-CT (p < 0.0001). Conclusions In non-contrast whole-body imaging of patients with multiple myeloma, the evaluated PCCT system provided superior image quality and significantly lower radiation-dose indices than the historical EID-CT system. These findings reflect the combined performance of the imaging systems and their respective acquisition and reconstruction settings.

title: Multifocal intradural extramedullary myxopapillary ependymoma of the spine.
abstract: Background Myxopapillary ependymoma (MPE) is an uncommon spinal ependymal tumor that usually arises as a solitary intradural extramedullary (IDEM) lesion in the conus medullaris, cauda equina, or filum terminale. MPE is designated WHO grade 2 since the 2021. Synchronous multifocal spinal MPE at initial presentation is rare and creates uncertainty regarding the extent and timing of surgery. Case presentation A 34-year-old man with no significant medical history presented with sudden severe non-radicular low-back pain and no neurological deficit. Contrast-enhanced MRI of the brain and entire spine showed multiple enhancing IDEM lesions confined to the lumbosacral region (T12-L1, L2, L3-L4, L4-L5, and S1). The dominant right-sided T12-L1 lesion markedly compressed the conus medullaris/proximal cauda equina. Complete microsurgical resection of this lesion was performed, and histopathology confirmed MPE, WHO grade 2 (Ki-67 ≤ 2-3%). The patient declined radiation-oncology referral, and the remaining lesions were monitored with MRI and CSF cytology, which remained negative. Nine months later, he developed paresthesias and recurrent low-back pain, with enlargement of the L3-L4 and L4-L5 lesions. Both were completely resected in a second operation, while the stable L2 and S1 lesions were left in place. No new neurological deficit occurred after either operation. The patient subsequently underwent radiation-oncology evaluation and received radiotherapy, and the residual lesions were unchanged at 3 months. Conclusion Multifocal spinal MPE may require individualized, staged management. Prioritizing symptomatic or compressive lesions can achieve decompression and tissue diagnosis while limiting multilevel surgical morbidity. Residual disease warrants long-term imaging surveillance, CSF assessment, and evaluation for radiotherapy.

title: Preoperative endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) strain elastography for the prediction of intraoperative pancreatic texture after pancreaticoduodenectomy: a prospective diagnostic accuracy study with exploratory analysis of clinically relevant postoperative pancreatic fistula.
abstract: Background Postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF) is the most serious complication of pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD); established risk tools require intraoperative variables. We assessed the diagnostic accuracy of preoperative endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) strain elastography for intraoperative pancreatic texture and, exploratorily, predictors of clinically relevant POPF (CR-POPF). Methods Prospective single-centre study of 100 consecutive patients undergoing elective PD. The index test was preoperative EUS strain ratio (SR), threshold ≤ 2.5 prespecified before enrolment; the reference standard was intraoperative texture recorded independently by two blinded surgeons, with neck-margin fibrosis grade as secondary reference. CR-POPF (ISGPS 2016 Grade B/C) was adjudicated blind to EUS. Accuracy is reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs). An exploratory index used Firth-penalised regression restricted to preoperative variables, with bootstrap validation. Reporting follows STARD, TRIPOD, and STROBE. Results Soft texture occurred in 58 (58%). SR ≤ 2.5 gave 51 true positives, 7 false positives, 7 false negatives, 35 true negatives: sensitivity 87.9% (95% CI 77.1-94.0), specificity 83.3% (69.4-91.7), predictive values 87.9 and 83.3%, accuracy 86.0% (77.9-91.5), and area under the curve (AUC) 0.91 (0.84-0.96). SR rose monotonically with fibrosis grade (2.0 ± 0.6 to 5.8 ± 1.9; Spearman ρ = +0.82, p < 0.001); mean histogram elasticity fell (ρ = - 0.79, p < 0.001). CR-POPF occurred in 16 (16%). Non-PDAC pathology was unassociated with CR-POPF (9/48 vs 7/52; odds ratio 1.48, 0.51-4.35; p = 0.59). Six preoperative variables were entered simultaneously (EUS-SR, duct diameter, albumin, haemoglobin, body mass index, serum amylase; amylase carried zero points in the rounded score). Apparent AUC was 0.87 (0.79-0.94), optimism-corrected 0.78, calibration slope 0.72, and Brier score 0.096. Conclusions Preoperative EUS strain elastography at a prespecified threshold identified intraoperative pancreatic texture accurately and tracked histological fibrosis, supporting it as an objective surrogate for parenchymal consistency. The index rests on 16 events, is hypothesis-generating, and requires external multicentre validation.

title: Opportunistic PSA testing is not the safe alternative : Why Austria's non-policy on prostate cancer screening maximizes harm and forfeits the benefits.
abstract: Austria has never implemented an organized prostate cancer screening program, yet opportunistic PSA testing has been widespread for more than three decades. This has produced the harms of screening without the safeguards of a program: testing outside appropriate age and life-expectancy windows, repeated testing of low-risk men, unnecessary biopsy, overdiagnosis and overtreatment, while generating little systematic information on quality or outcomes. Randomized evidence shows that organized, repeated screening can reduce prostate cancer mortality substantially, whereas opportunistic testing delivers less benefit with more overdiagnosis. Contemporary risk-adapted pathways further improve the balance of benefit and harm: defined start and stop ages, PSA-based risk stratification, MRI before biopsy, targeted biopsy, and active surveillance can reduce unnecessary biopsies and detection or treatment of indolent disease without compromising detection of clinically significant cancer. Europe has therefore moved toward organized, PSA-based screening with MRI as a follow-up test. Austria is now participating in PRAISE-U Plus and has initiated a national multidisciplinary consensus process involving 65 experts from 22 organizations. The policy question is no longer whether Austrian men are being screened-they are-but whether screening remains unstructured or becomes organized, quality-assured and equitable. The evidence supports the latter: invite the right men, stratify risk, biopsy selectively, treat only clinically relevant disease, and measure outcomes systematically.

title: Intraoperative bedside lung-ultrasound use to optimize positive end-expiratory pressure for elective robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy or cystectomy: a randomized clinical trial.
abstract: Purpose This study evaluated efficacy and safety of intraoperative individualized stepwise positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) titration guided by lung ultrasound (LUS) in reducing pulmonary atelectasis and complications in patients undergoing robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy or cystectomy (RARPC). Methods This randomized trial included 88 patients undergoing elective RARPC. Patients were assigned to either standard ventilation (PEEP 4 cmH₂O; group C) or LUS-guided stepwise PEEP titration up to 12 cmH₂O (group R). Patients, outcome assessors, and the data analyst were blinded. The primary outcome was analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model, estimating the between-group difference in LUS score at 2 h after surgery. Results Group R showed significantly lower total LUS scores at 2 h after surgery (adjusted difference: -1.68, 95%CI: -2.89 to -0.47; p = 0.007) compared to group C. Likewise, significantly lower LUS scores were observed in Group R from the end of surgery onward. PEEP titration progressively reduced post-pneumoperitoneum atelectasis rates from 50% to 9.1%, at a highest PEEP level of 12 cmH₂O. Dynamic lung compliance in group R was significantly greater at Top compared with the control group (58.93 ± 3.48 vs. 49.91 ± 5.74 mL/cmH₂O; p < 0.001). Heart rate, mean arterial pressure, oxygen saturation, and end-tidal CO₂ were comparable at all time points. Both groups were comparable for intraoperative hypotension and bradycardia. Conclusion Intraoperative LUS-guided individualized PEEP optimization significantly reduced the incidence of postoperative atelectasis and improved dynamic lung compliance without compromising hemodynamic stability in patients undergoing RARPC. Lung ultrasound offers a practical, effective, and non-invasive bedside tool for optimizing ventilation in high-risk surgical settings. Trial registration and protocol This study was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov in March 2024 (ID: NCT06307704). The trial protocol is available through the ClinicalTrials.gov registry at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06307704 .

title: Lamina bone regeneration and recurrent lumbar spinal stenosis: associated factors and transcriptomic analysis of excessive bone regeneration.
abstract: Objective To investigate the association between lamina bone regeneration and recurrent lumbar spinal stenosis (rLSS), its associated factors, and the potential molecular mechanisms. Methods This retrospective study included 241 patients with single-level lumbar spinal stenosis who underwent laminotomy decompression at the First Affiliated Hospital of Shihezi University between July 2016 and July 2023. Baseline and surgical data were collected. The interlaminar space area was measured on CT and MRI, and the final lamina bone regeneration rate was calculated. Clinical outcomes and symptom recurrence were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), modified MacNab criteria, and Self-Paced Walking Test (SPWT). Peripheral blood RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analysis were performed in patients with excessive bone regeneration, and differentially expressed genes were validated by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). LASSO regression, multivariable logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis were performed using R software and GraphPad Prism 9.5. A P-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results A total of 241 patients were included, with a mean follow-up of 4.69 ± 2.25 years. The incidence of rLSS was 9.96% (24/241). The rLSS group had a significantly smaller preoperative interlaminar space area and a significantly higher final lamina bone regeneration rate than the Non-rLSS group (both P < 0.05). LASSO regression identified surgical segment, preoperative interlaminar space area, and final lamina bone regeneration rate as factors associated with rLSS. Multivariable logistic regression showed that a higher final bone regeneration rate (OR = 1.091, P < 0.001), a smaller preoperative interlaminar space area (OR = 0.982, P = 0.040), and a lower surgical segment (OR = 6.142, P = 0.005) were associated with rLSS. ROC analysis showed that the final lamina bone regeneration rate yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.812 (95% CI, 0.704-0.921) for distinguishing rLSS from Non-rLSS, with a cutoff value of 34.93, a sensitivity of 0.708, and a specificity of 0.825. The excessive bone regeneration group (n = 41) had a significantly smaller preoperative interlaminar space area than the normal group (n = 200) (P < 0.05). LASSO regression identified preoperative interlaminar space area, intraoperative blood loss, and a history of osteoarthritis as candidate associated factors. In multivariable analysis, only preoperative interlaminar space area remained an independent factor (OR = 0.989, P = 0.017). The AUC of preoperative interlaminar space area for distinguishing excessive bone regeneration was 0.634 (95% CI, 0.547-0.721). Peripheral blood RNA-seq and RT-qPCR showed that the expression levels of SPARC, ALPL, SMAD1, and BMP2 were upregulated in patients with excessive bone regeneration. Differentially expressed genes were enriched in the Hippo, FoxO, TGF-β, and Wnt signaling pathways. Conclusions A small preoperative interlaminar space area, a high lamina bone regeneration rate, and a lower surgical segment were associated with rLSS. Preoperative interlaminar space area is associated with excessive lamina bone regeneration. SPARC, ALPL, SMAD1, BMP2, and the Hippo, FoxO, TGF-β, and Wnt signaling pathways may be involved in the underlying molecular mechanisms.

title: Feasibility of a lumbar CT-to-MRI image translation framework using a conditional CycleGANs for fracture stage determination in osteoporotic compression fractures.
abstract: Purpose Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides a reliable indicator of fracture stage. However, MRI scans can be expensive, time-consuming, and not readily accessible to all patients. With recent advances in artificial intelligence, translating lumbar CT images into MRI images has become feasible using cycle generative adversarial network (CycleGANs) based approaches. The aim of this study was to evaluate the feasibility of a model that translates lumbar CT images into MRI images (T1-weighted contrast-enhanced sequences) to predict the stage of osteoporotic compression fracture (OCFs) using conditional CycleGANs. Methods A total of 652 patients diagnosed with OCFs who underwent both CT and MRI within 2 weeks were retrospectively collected. Of these, 552 patients were used for training, and an independent set of 100 patients was reserved for testing. CT and MRI volumes were aligned using segmentation-based rigid registration. The proposed framework consisted of two stages: generation of vertebra-specific acute fracture maps from CT images using a 3D ResNet-based model, followed by CT-to-MRI image translation using a 3D conditional CycleGANs with acute stage conditioning. Performance was evaluated using vertebra-level classification metrics, image similarity metrics, and qualitative assessment by five experienced readers, including three spine neurosurgeons, one orthopedic spine specialist, and one radiologist. Results Fractures were most common at the thoracolumbar junction. A total of 800 vertebral bodies were analyzed. Of 678 non-acute OCFs, 667 were correctly classified and 11 were misclassified as acute; of 122 acute OCFs, 106 were correctly identified and 16 were misclassified as non-acute. Acute fracture classification achieved a precision of 0.906, recall of 0.869, and F1-score of 0.887. Synthetic MRI images showed modest quantitative agreement with real MRI (Normalized MAE 0.094 ± 0.024; PSNR 18.7 ± 1.7 dB; SSIM 0.38 ± 0.04). Qualitative evaluation demonstrated high similarity in vertebral body morphology at the fracture level, with mean similarity scores of 87.2% for the conditional CycleGAN and 85.3% for the conventional CycleGAN. Conclusions This study demonstrates the feasibility of a lumbar CT-to-MRI image translation framework using a conditional CycleGAN for determining fracture stage.

title: Radiological assessment of navigated pedicle screw placement in the cervical spine: a comparative evaluation of a novel orthogonal view evaluation method (ovem) versus other classification systems (Neo/Modified Gertzbein-Robbins/Wiesner).
abstract: Study design A retrospective, comparison study. Purpose This study compares different computed tomography (CT)-based methods for evaluating the postoperative position of cervical pedicle screws (CPS). Specifically, our novel Orthogonal View Evaluation Method (OVEM) alongside the Neo, modified Gerzbein-Robbins, and Wiesner classifications to validate a standardized system for postoperative assessment of screw placement in the cervical spine. Methods All enrolled patients underwent navigated, posterior stabilization using CPS in the subaxial spine (C3-C6). The intra- and inter-observer assessment was carried out using two statistical methods: the Fleiss Kappa and the Gwet´s agreement coefficient (Gwet´s AC1). Results A total of 90 (60 men and 30 women) patients with total number of screws 275 (median 2, IQR 2 to 4) were enrolled in the study. title: Systemic immune-inflammation index predicts neurological recovery in degenerative cervical myelopathy: a comparative analysis of OPLL and non-OPLL patients.
abstract: Purpose To compare systemic inflammatory characteristics between patients with ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament (OPLL) and non-OPLL degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM) and to evaluate the prognostic value of the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), alone and in combination with radiological parameters, for postoperative neurological recovery. Methods This retrospective prognostic cohort study included 317 surgically treated patients with DCM (98 with OPLL and 219 without OPLL) with complete 2-year follow-up data. Neurological and clinical outcomes were assessed using the visual analog scale (VAS), Neck Disability Index (NDI), modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association (mJOA) score, and mJOA recovery rate; patients were categorized as having favorable recovery (mJOA recovery rate ≥ 50%; n = 231) or unfavorable recovery (< 50%; n = 86). Preoperative hematologic inflammatory indices, including the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and SII, serum biochemical profiles, surgical characteristics, and cervical radiological parameters were collected. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was used to assess maximum spinal cord compression (MSCC), maximum canal compromise (MCC), transverse area (TA), and compression ratio (CR). Full multivariable logistic regression models identified factors independently associated with favorable recovery. Sensitivity analyses separately adjusted for surgical approach, surgical procedure, and the numbers of decompressed and fused levels. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses assessed discriminative performance and optimal cutoffs. Predictors that remained independently associated with favorable recovery in the full multivariable models were retained, and parsimonious logistic regression models were refitted for ROC analysis, nomogram construction, and internal validation. The combined scores represented weighted linear predictors from the corresponding refitted SII-TA models and were not predicted probabilities. Internal validation was performed using 1,000 bootstrap resamples; calibration was assessed using calibration curves and the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and clinical net benefit was evaluated using decision curve analysis. Results Patients with OPLL had significantly higher white blood cell (WBC) counts and SII values than those without OPLL. In the overall cohort, lower SII and larger TA were independently associated with favorable neurological recovery. A combined predictive score was derived from the refitted parsimonious model as follows: Score = - 0.202 + 5.697 × TA - 0.294 × (SII/100). Score ≥ 0.50 was identified as the optimal cutoff for predicting favorable neurological recovery. ROC analysis further identified cutoff values of SII ≤ 556.5 and TA ≥ 0.405 cm² as predictors of favorable outcomes. Subgroup analyses suggested differing predictor patterns between the OPLL and non-OPLL groups. In the OPLL subgroup, lower SII remained independently associated with favorable neurological recovery, with an optimal cutoff value of SII ≤ 558.4. In contrast, in patients with non-OPLL DCM, a distinct combined predictive score was derived from the refitted parsimonious model: Score = - 0.453 + 5.522 × TA - 0.210 × (SII/100). Score ≥ 0.99 was identified as the optimal cutoff for predicting favorable neurological recovery. Corresponding ROC-derived thresholds of SII ≤ 390.6 and TA ≥ 0.445 cm² were identified for predicting favorable neurological recovery in this subgroup. The association between lower SII and favorable recovery remained significant after separate adjustment for each surgical characteristic. The optimism-corrected areas under the ROC curve were 0.749, 0.711, and 0.722 for the overall DCM, OPLL, and non-OPLL DCM models, respectively; goodness-of-fit tests did not indicate lack of fit, and decision curve analysis suggested potential clinical net benefit. Conclusion Systemic inflammatory burden, quantified by SII, was independently associated with long-term neurological recovery in patients with DCM. Subgroup analyses yielded different predictor patterns and SII cutoff estimates in the OPLL and non-OPLL groups; however, these findings should be considered exploratory and require external confirmation. Models integrating systemic inflammatory and radiological parameters may assist risk stratification, but their clinical utility should be established in independent prospective cohorts before implementation.

title: Cage rotation and effective rim support are associated with subsidence after TLIF using a single expandable banana-shaped cage design.
abstract: Purpose To determine whether postoperative cage obliquity and vertebral rim support are associated with 12-month subsidence after TLIF using a single articulating expandable banana-shaped cage design. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 101 patients (109 levels) treated with an articulating expandable banana-shaped cage. Postoperative CT was used to measure cage obliquity angle and cage-rim contact ratio. Subsidence was defined as ≥ 2 mm at 12 months. Spearman correlations were used to examine relationships between cage obliquity and rim-support metrics. Associations of cage obliquity and cage-rim contact with subsidence were evaluated using separate multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for Hounsfield units. Spatial heatmaps visualized the distribution of anterior rim support, which was further quantified using mediolateral contact metrics. Results Subsidence occurred in 16 levels (14.7%). Greater cage obliquity angle was associated with subsidence (OR 1.40 per 5°, 95% CI 1.10-1.84, p = 0.004), whereas greater cage-rim contact ratio was inversely associated with subsidence (OR 0.68 per 10%, 95% CI 0.51-0.90, p = 0.008). Cage obliquity was inversely correlated with cage-rim contact ratio (ρ = -0.370; p < 0.001) and mediolateral contact spread (ρ = -0.457; p < 0.001), but not with contact centroid. Fusion, radiographic correction loss, and patient-reported outcomes did not differ significantly by subsidence status. Conclusions In this single-design cohort, greater residual cage obliquity and reduced cage-rim contact ratio were associated with subsidence, identifying insufficient rotation and reduced effective anterior rim support as potentially modifiable technical factors. These findings provide a rationale for developing and prospectively evaluating intraoperative methods to assess cage rotation and optimize rim support, although the optimal rotational target and its preventive effect require further validation.

title: Atypical-laterality curve patterns in adult idiopathic scoliosis: refining the AdIS classification.
abstract: Purpose The objective of this study was to analyze the distribution of curve patterns in adult idiopathic scoliosis (AdIS) patients according to the AdIS classification by Lin et al. We also aim to identify the prevalence of atypical curve patterns that are not represented within the existing framework and propose a laterality modifier as an extension of the AdIS classification. Methods Adult idiopathic scoliosis patients aged above 18 years who underwent posterior spinal fusion (PSF) between 2023 and 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. Radiographic parameters were measured using pre-operative whole spine radiographs. Curves were classified according to AdIS classification by Lin et. al. Reversed curve patterns not represented by the current AdIS classification were recorded as atypical-laterality variants with an added laterality modifier, denoted "R" (reversed). Descriptive statistical analysis was performed. Results A total of 215 patients were included. The existing AdIS classification successfully classified 92.6% of patients, whereas 7.4% exhibited atypical-laterality curve patterns. AdIS type 1 curves were the most prevalent (34.7%), followed by type 2 (17.6%) and type 6 (15.1%). The majority of curves demonstrated non-structural lumbosacral modifiers (89.4%) and preserved global alignment (98.0%). Among the atypical-laterality cases, AdIS 6-R and 5-R curves were the most numerically frequent subtypes, accounting for five (31.3%) and four (25.0%) cases respectively. Conclusion The AdIS classification demonstrated excellent applicability, successfully classifying 92.6% of patients in our study cohort. Atypical-laterality patterns were identified in 16 patients (7.4%), with AdIS 6-R being the commonest pattern encountered.

title: Postoperative opioid usage in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: a comparative study of vertebral body tethering and posterior spinal fusion.
abstract: Purpose The objective of this study is to compare opioid utilization throughout the postoperative period between patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) treated with either vertebral body tethering (VBT) or posterior spinal fusion (PSF). The secondary purpose was to identify risk factors associated with postoperative opioid use for patients undergoing VBT. Methods This was a single center, retrospective cohort study including patients with AIS who underwent primary surgical treatment through either a PSF or VBT approach from 2012 to 2023. Outcome measures of interest include baseline demographic information, opioid characteristics, operative information, complications, and radiographic measurements. Given the discrepancy in pain management protocols within the time period VBT was introduced, a separate same era sensitivity analysis was conducted assessing characteristics of opioid utilization from patients operated from 2019 to 2023. An additional sub-analysis was performed evaluating the VBT cohort to identify individual risk factors associated with postoperative opioid use. Continuous variables were compared using independent samples t-test and categorical variables were analyzed using chi-square testing. Statistical significance for these tests was set to p < 0.05. Binary logistic regression was also performed for the VBT sub-analysis to calculate odds ratios for significant variables of interest. Results 364 patients (118 VBT; 246 PSF) met the cohort criteria. Gender, height and skeletal maturity were not significantly different between groups (p > 0.05). Patients in the PSF group were older (14.9 vs. 16.1 years, p < 0.001) with a higher body mass index at baseline than VBT patients (20.8 vs. 21.8 kg/m 2 , p = 0.011). Estimated blood loss, intraoperative blood product use, and days with drain in place were greater in the PSF group compared to the VBT group (all p < 0.05). While PSF led to greater correction of main thoracic curves and coronal balance (both p < 0.05), VBT patients experienced a greater postoperative correction in L5 tilt angle, lumbar lordosis, pelvic incidence-lumbar lordosis mismatch and cSVA compared to the PSF group (all p < 0.05). In the primary comparison, PSF patients required opioids for a significantly longer time compared to their VBT counterparts following surgery (1.8 vs. 1.3 months, p = 0.002). Despite lack of statistical significance, same-era sensitivity analysis described similar differences in postoperative opioid use duration between groups (1.6 months vs. 1.3 months, p = 0.086). Sub-analysis of VBT patients revealed that body mass index was significantly greater in the group of operated patients that required opioids than those who did not, as each unit increase in BMI led to a 1.3 greater odds of postoperative opioid usage (OR = 1.3 [CI 1.1-1.4], p = 0.002). Conclusion VBT was associated with a shorter period of opioid-level pain management postoperatively than PSF patients and displayed improvement in sagittal radiographic parameters. Furthermore, increased BMI was identified as a significant risk factor for opioid usage in VBT patients during the perioperative period.

title: Paraspinal muscle radiomics from MRI alone or combined with CT for predicting outcomes after degenerative lumbar spine surgery: a scoping review.
abstract: Purpose Paraspinal muscle degeneration is increasingly recognised as a predictor of outcomes following lumbar spine surgery. This review maps studies that used paraspinal muscle radiomics, alone or within multimodal models, to predict postoperative outcomes in lumbar degenerative disease, and appraises their methodological quality and risk of bias. Methods This scoping review followed PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Embase, Scopus and Web of Science were searched from inception to 10 April 2026. Eligible studies extracted radiomic or deep features from paraspinal muscles on preoperative MRI, with or without other tissues, modalities or clinical variables, and reported the discrimination of a model predicting a postoperative outcome. Data was charted with CHARMS-based items, quality was appraised with METRICS and risk of bias with PROBAST+AI. Findings were synthesised by clinical question, and MRI-only muscle models were presented separately from multimodal models. Results Six retrospective cohort studies were included, of which three addressed functional improvement and one study each evaluated recurrent disc herniation, radiographic adjacent segment degeneration and prolonged length of stay. Only two studies performed external validation: combined models achieved areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.79-0.80 for functional outcome after open fusion and 0.835 for radiographic adjacent segment degeneration. Internally validated AUCs of final models ranged from 0.76 to 0.94 and depended on the resampling design. In the largest cohort, adding radiomics to clinical predictors significantly improved discrimination. In two others, incremental value was limited: radiomics added only a small gain over conventional fatty infiltration (AUC 0.922 to 0.936), and adding clinical and disc features did not improve a muscle radiomics model (0.814 vs 0.862; p = 0.083). Calibration was assessed in five studies, and none reported calibration slope or intercept. METRICS quality was good in four studies and moderate in two; under PROBAST+AI, five studies were judged at high concern or high risk of bias and one unclear. Conclusion Paraspinal muscle radiomics from routine preoperative imaging is a promising way to predict outcomes after surgery for lumbar degenerative disease, using scans that patients already have. However, the evidence comes from a small number of heterogeneous retrospective studies, mostly at high risk of bias, with limited assessment of calibration and inconsistent incremental value over conventional measures. The models remain investigational, but prospective multicentre studies with rigorous pipelines, standardised outcomes, clinical comparators, external validation, calibration and decision-curve analysis could move them towards clinical use.

title: Machine learning-based differentiation of congenital and adolescent idiopathic scoliosis using routine radiographic parameters.
abstract: Purpose Accurate differentiation of congenital scoliosis (CS) from adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is important for appropriate diagnostic evaluation and subsequent imaging work-up. We evaluated machine learning models using routinely available demographic and radiographic variables to distinguish CS from AIS. Methods In this retrospective single-center study, 166 pediatric patients with scoliosis who underwent standing radiography and MRI between 2018 and 2025 were included. Etiological classification was based on clinical and imaging findings, including whole-spine MRI. Demographic and conventional radiographic variables were used to develop Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, and k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) models. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), calibration analysis, decision curve analysis, and SHAP-based interpretability. Results Of the 166 patients, 96 (57.8%) had AIS and 70 (42.2%) had congenital scoliosis. Logistic Regression achieved the highest overall accuracy (79.4%), whereas Random Forest demonstrated the highest discriminative performance (ROC-AUC, 0.829). Pairwise comparisons using the DeLong test showed no statistically significant differences between the evaluated models. SHAP analysis identified Cobb angle, age, vertebral level, and Nash-Moe rotation grade as the most influential predictors. Calibration performance varied across models, while decision curve analysis demonstrated the greatest net benefit for Logistic Regression. Conclusion Machine learning models demonstrated moderate diagnostic performance in differentiating congenital scoliosis from AIS. However, their limited sensitivity and potential for false-negative predictions preclude independent clinical use. Larger studies and external validation are required before their potential role as adjunctive decision-support tools can be established.

title: Accuracy of anatomical landmarks for the pelvic C-clamp: a three-dimensional CT imaging study.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the accuracy of three commonly used anatomical landmarks for pelvic C-clamp pin insertion using three-dimensional (3D) CT imaging. Methods From a cohort of patients undergoing CT angiography of the lower extremities, 3D bony reconstruction images were created. Three commonly used anatomical insertion landmarks-the intersection points described by Ganz et al. (point A), by Pohlemann et al. (point B), and by the DePuy Synthes Pelvic C-Clamp surgical guide (point C)-were drawn on the 3D CT reconstruction images, and their relationship with the SI joint surface was recorded. We additionally stratified landmark accuracy by SI joint surface morphology. Patient-level clustering was accounted for using generalized estimating equations (GEE). Results A total of 101 hemipelves were obtained from 51 patients (36 men and 15 women; mean age 61.56 years). In terms of accuracy, point A demonstrated 69.31% of points overlying the SI surface, recorded as 'IN', and 22.77% overlying the central quadrant of the SI surface, recorded as 'CENTER'; point B demonstrated 68.32% and 21.78%; and point C demonstrated 56.44% and 9.90%, respectively. Point A demonstrated significantly higher odds than point C for both 'IN' (OR 1.74, 95% CI 1.03-2.95; p = 0.0377) and 'CENTER' placement (OR 2.69, 95% CI 1.07-6.76; p = 0.0358), whereas the corresponding differences for point B did not reach statistical significance ('IN': OR 1.67, 95% CI 0.99-2.79; p = 0.0534; 'CENTER': OR 2.54, 95% CI 0.91-7.10; p = 0.0761). Anterior misplacement was the most frequent type of malposition for all insertion points. Sacral morphology did not statistically influence the accuracy of any landmark. Conclusion Point A demonstrated the highest observed imaging-defined accuracy and significantly higher odds of both IN and CENTER placement than point C after accounting for patient-level clustering. Point B showed higher odds than point C for both outcomes, but these differences did not reach statistical significance. These findings should be interpreted as bone-referenced, imaging-based estimates rather than direct evidence of biomechanical superiority or clinical safety. Fluoroscopic guidance remains advisable when clinically feasible. Level of evidence III Diagnostic Level III.

title: Surgical outcomes of single-stage posterior debridement combined with titanium mesh cage reconstruction and bone grafting for spinal infection after vertebral augmentation: a multicenter study.
abstract: Purpose To investigate the surgical outcomes of single-stage posterior debridement combined with titanium mesh cage (TMC) reconstruction and bone grafting in the treatment of spinal infection following percutaneous vertebral augmentation (VA). Methods A multicenter retrospective study was conducted, including patients who underwent surgery for spinal infection after percutaneous VA for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCF) between January 2018 and December 2023. All patients received single-stage posterior debridement, TMC reconstruction, and bone grafting. Operative duration, intraoperative blood loss, and clinical outcomes-including preoperative, immediate postoperative, and final follow-up visual analogue scale (VAS) scores, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and local kyphotic Cobb angles-were recorded and analyzed. Results A total of 51 patients (17 male, 34 female; mean age: 68.35 ± 6.83 years) were enrolled, of whom 49 completed follow-up and were included in the final analysis; two patients died during follow-up and were treated as missing data. The average interval between VA and revision surgery was 7.51 ± 5.77 months. The preoperative American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) grade was C, D, and E in 2, 40, and 9 patients, respectively. The average operation time was 201.33 ± 84.38 min, with a mean intraoperative blood loss of 900.98 ± 507.99 mL. Pathogens were detected in 31 cases postoperatively. The mean follow-up duration was 19.65 ± 4.56 months. At the final follow-up of the 49 patients, VAS scores, ODI, and local Cobb angles significantly improved compared to preoperative values (P < 0.05). Bony fusion was achieved in 45 of the 49 patients (91.8%), with an average duration of 5.44 ± 1.18 months. Conclusion Single-stage posterior debridement combined with TMC reconstruction and bone grafting was associated with favorable clinical and radiographic outcomes in patients with spinal infection following percutaneous VA.

title: Obturator internus muscle entrapment in posterior wall acetabular fractures: two cases with preoperative and intraoperative findings.
abstract: Introduction We report two cases of the rare presentation of obturator internus muscle (OI) entrapment in posterior wall fractures of the acetabulum. Although piriformis muscle entrapment has been previously reported, to the best of our knowledge, OI entrapment associated with posterior wall acetabular fractures has not been previously documented. Case presentation Case 1: A 38-year-old male presented with right hip and knee pain following a road traffic accident. He was diagnosed with a posterior hip dislocation, posterior wall and posterior column fractures of the acetabulum, and a posterior knee dislocation. During surgery, the OI muscle was found interposed between the displaced posterior wall fragment and the remaining posterior column. Case 2: A 43-year-old male sustained blunt abdominal trauma and a Pipkin type IV injury involving a femoral head fracture associated with a posterior wall acetabular fracture following a road traffic accident. After stabilisation of the abdominal injury with laparoscopic repair of the mesenteric injury, the patient underwent open reduction and internal fixation of the posterior wall fracture, along with removal of intra-articular fragments associated with an infra-foveal femoral head fracture. Intraoperatively, the OI muscle was similarly found interposed between the displaced posterior wall fragment and the remaining posterior column. In both cases, retrospective review of the preoperative CT images demonstrated OI interposition corresponding to the intraoperative findings. Both patients followed a standard postoperative rehabilitation protocol. At the one-year follow-up, both patients had satisfactory clinical outcomes, with Merle d'Aubigné-Postel scores of 16 and 17 and Harris Hip Scores of 92.7 and 93 for Cases 1 and 2, respectively. Neither patient showed radiographic evidence of post-traumatic arthritis. Conclusion These cases highlight the importance of recognising OI muscle entrapment as a potential cause of difficulty in reducing posterior wall acetabular fractures. Careful evaluation of preoperative CT images, particularly using soft-tissue window settings, may facilitate the identification of OI interposition. Intraoperatively, failure to identify the OI tendon between the superior and inferior gemelli, when both are clearly identified, should raise suspicion of entrapment. Meticulous identification of soft-tissue structures may help achieve anatomical fracture reduction and successful fixation.

title: Probe-mediated subcellular organelles translocation enabled ratiometric quantification of nitroreductase activity and microviscosity for hypoxia imaging and precise tumor delineation.
abstract: Quantitative assessment of hypoxia-induced nitroreductase (NTR) upregulation and pathological viscosity elevation offers a critical diagnostic parameter for precise cancer diagnostics.​ We propose a subcellular organelle translocation strategy for ultrasensitive quantification of NTR/microviscosity and subsequent precise evaluation of tumor hypoxia levels. The constructed NTR-sensitive probe Cy826 releases the fluorophore Cy468 upon NTR catalysis, accompanied by a significant fluorescence turn-on response (21.9-fold enhancement) and subcellular organelle translocation from endoplasmic reticulum (ER) to lysosomes, which effectively reduced local probe accumulation and significantly alleviated the aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) effect and spectral crosstalk in quantification process. The cyclen-based hemicyanine Cy468 is a fluorophore distinct from our previously reported Cy496, with near-infrared (NIR) emission (~ 720 nm), lower logP, and lysosomal rather than mitochondrial targeting. Cy826 displays high sensitivity (LOD = 8.2 ng/mL) and excellent selectivity toward NTR, along with a strong fluorescence enhancement under high viscosity and molecular crowding conditions. The probe also facilitates real-time monitoring of viscosity changes in ER and lysosomes, and dynamically responds to endogenous NTR activity under varying hypoxia levels. Moreover, after administration of Cy826, the considerable tumor-to-background ratio (TBR > 12) enables high-contrast imaging of hypoxic tumors from early to advanced stages with favorable biocompatibility and metabolic characteristics. Our subcellular organelle translocation strategy proposed in this study offers a novel approach to mitigating ACQ effect in quantification assignment, and the high-performance NIR fluorescent probe drafted in this work provides a prospective tool for precise tumor diagnosis and intraoperative navigation via multi-parameter imaging of hypoxic tumor microenvironment.

title: Three-dimensional evaluation of maxillary sinus volume and nasal septal deviation after surgically assisted rapid maxillary expansion with and without pterygomaxillary disjunction.
abstract: Objectives This study aimed to compare changes in maxillary sinus volume and nasal septal deviation after surgically assisted rapid maxillary expansion (SARME) with and without pterygomaxillary disjunction (PMD) using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). Materials and methods This retrospective study included 24 patients whose skeletal maturation had been determined during the preoperative orthodontic assessment based on hand-wrist radiography together with evaluation of midpalatal suture maturation on CBCT images, had undergone SARME, and had suitable preoperative CBCT scans and postoperative CBCT scans obtained 6-12 months after surgery. Patients were classified as PMD+ or PMD- according to the surgical procedure documented in the operative records (n=12 per group). Maxillary sinus volume was assessed by semi-automatic segmentation using 3D Slicer software. Nasal septal deviation was measured on coronal CBCT images. Preoperative-to-postoperative changes (T0 to T1) and between-group differences were evaluated using mixed-design ANOVA (p<0.05). Results Maxillary sinus volume increased significantly​ in both groups after SARME (p<0.001)​. Total maxillary sinus volume, averaged across the preoperative and postoperative measurements, did not differ significantly between the PMD+ and PMD- groups (p<=<0.171). However, the preoperative-to-postoperative increase (T0 to T1) was greater in the PMD+ group (time × group interaction, p<0.001). Nasal septal deviation decreased significantly in both groups after surgery (p<0.001). The time × group interaction for nasal septal deviation was not significant (p=0.535). Conclusions After SARME, maxillary sinus volume increased and nasal septal deviation decreased in both groups. The preoperative-to-postoperative increase in maxillary sinus volume was greater in the PMD+ group, whereas the change in nasal septal deviation did not differ significantly between groups. Clinical relevance These findings may contribute to treatment planning by clarifying the association between pterygomaxillary disjunction and postoperative morphological changes in maxillary sinus volume and nasal septal deviation after SARME.
